PREAMBLE We, Eagle-Members of the Fraternal Order of Eagles – Philippine Eagles, Incorporated (TFOEPE, Inc.), united by a unique bond of communal fraternal organization and anchored on Four (4)
Pillars of Eagleism --- Brotherhood, Service, Unity and Divine Power with the guiding principles of --- “Service Through Strong Brotherhood” and Deo et Patria which means for God and Country - form a strong, first Philippine born fraternal sociocivic organization that will serve a Supreme Being and cares for humanity at all times, do hereby promulgate this Philippine Eagles Constitution and its corresponding By-Laws.

--- Page 27 ---
ARTICLE I
PHILIPPINE EAGLES CONSTITUTION AND BY-LAWS
SECTION 1. The Philippine Eagles Constitution. The Fraternal Order of Eagles - Philippine Eagles, Incorporated (TFOE-PE, Inc.), a nonstock corporation duly registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) under SEC Registration No. CN 2017-21277 is governed by its Eagles Constitution and SEC By-Laws to which every Eagle-member is enjoined to abide by and obey at all times. The Eagles Constitution and the corresponding By-Laws are ordained to guide the Philippine Eagles, regions, clubs and eagle-members thereof in the performance of their roles, duties, responsibilities and obligations in the Philippine Eagles, as well as in the conduct of their affairs internally and externally with fellow eagles.
SECTION 2. The Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024. The tenets and provisions of this Eagles Constitution shall be cited as the Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024.

--- Page 28 ---
ARTICLE II
NAME AND DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES,
PURPOSES AND GOALS
CHAPTER 11
NAME AND DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES
We, Eagle-members of The Fraternal Order of Eagles- Philippine Eagles, Incorporated (TFOE-PE, Inc.) and adjunct to The Fraternal Order of Philippine Eagles founded on June 22, 1979, declare:
SECTION 1. Name and Identity. We shall call ourselves the Philippine Eagles and shall name our Fraternity as The Fraternal Order of Eagles - Philippine Eagles, Incorporated (TFOE-PE, Inc.) or briefly, the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 2. Declaration of Principles. The guiding principles of the Philippine Eagles shall be: “Service Through Strong Brotherhood”:
and *** DEO ET PATRIA which means FOR GOD AND COUNTRY ***
CHAPTER 2
DECLARATION OF PURPOSES AND GOALS
SECTION 1. Meaning of Eagles. The Philippine Eagles shall be:
E

-

Enlightened and innovative humanitarian

A

Animated primarily by a strong bond of brotherhood and fraternal ties

G -

God-loving, non-sectarian, non political

L

-

Law-abiding, liberty-oriented

E

-

Emblazed with intense mission of

S

-

Service to God, country and its people, above all.

THE HISTORICAL DECLARATION OF GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE FRATERNAL ORDER OF EAGLESPHILIPPINE EAGLES INC WAS RATIFIED ON JUNE 25, 1979 AT UP ASIAN INSTITUTE OF TOURISM, QUEZON CITY 1

--- Page 29 ---
SECTION 2. Declaration of Purposes and Goals. The Philippine Eagles, all regions, Eagles clubs, commissions, committees, bodies and eaglemembers shall achieve the following purposes and goals:
a. The Philippine Eagles shall evolve, establish and implement in the Philippines affiliated regions, Eagles clubs and in other countries a new approach and vision in the quality and scope of humanitarian service which they shall seek to rationalize for the benefit and human betterment of the Philippines and its community, in particular, or in other countries, in particular, where there is an affiliated Eagles Club or Region;
b. They shall encourage the formation and organization of Eagles clubs and regions in the Philippines and other countries;
c. They shall provide means for community outreach and venue for healthy fellowship through various programs and humanitarian services among others;
d. They shall encourage exchange of ideas, business, professional, cultural, social and other opportunities and advantages for the benefits of eagle-members, Eagles clubs and regions of the Philippine Eagles;
e. They shall promote health research, scientific inquiries, educational and social legislation and shall provide forum for their open discussions. They shall not debate or discuss partisan politics and religion in the Eagles clubs and regions, committees, commissions and bodies of the Philippine Eagles; f.

They shall be governed by this Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024 and guided by the SEC By-Laws and the amendments thereof including acts and resolutions duly enacted by the National Assembly, when warranted, which shall be uniform for all the Eagle-members and in all levels of the Philippine Eagles;

--- Page 30 ---
g. They shall resolve their internal problems and affairs within the Philippine Eagles initially and only after exhaustion of administrative remedy, they shall recourse to the courts of law for civil or criminal cases, if warranted. This gesture of exhaustion of administrative remedy shall be part of their Oath not to embarrass the Philippine Eagles, Region or the Eagles Club by taking any action outside the remedy provided by the National Fraternity, Region or Eagles Club on any matter which might arise in their relationship with the Philippine Eagles, Region, Club or with Fellow Eagles; and
h. They shall try to help and come to aid to the Eagle-Members, less privileged and marginalized sectors as partner of the Government in nation building based on the concept and principle of Alalayang Agila.
SECTION 3. Desideratum. The Philippine Eagles whose nucleus has signed this declaration shall seek and construct their humanitarian service, usefulness and destiny in the Philippines geared to benefit primarily the less privileged and marginalized sector. They are strongly committed to render personal service for the betterment of the Eagle-Members, the regions or clubs affiliated and its Eaglemembers. They shall endeavor to achieve these goals through Service and Unity. They shall give no excuses as they have hereby set the innovative tone of change which shall present as a matter-of-fact by rendering humanitarian service to the less privileged and marginalized sector of the society, in the light of existing environment. They shall give dignity to endeavor by doing and practicing what they hereby strongly set and desire.
SECTION 4. The Eagle 2. The Eagle is a large specie of bird and regarded as a symbol of bold strength and courageous character. It is noted for its majestic and noble qualities and keen and bright foresight.
An Eagle who is humanitarian shall be endowed with the above qualities. He shall render personal service to his fellowmen and Note: The original declaration of objectives of the Fraternity was signed by the Founding Fathers of the Philippine Eagles on June 28, 1979 at the UP Asian Institute of Tourism, Diliman, Quezon City. The names of the Founding Fathers for historical reference are hereto attached as Appendix “G”.
2

--- Page 31 ---
community with dignity and nobility; he shall have the innovative spirit of courage and strength of rendering personal humanitarian service and the keen interest and perception of the long-range goals of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 5. Eagleism 3. As define, Eagleism is not found in any old or modern lexicon. Eagleism is unique and peculiar to the Philippine Eagles. Based on the 1989 Magna Carta Eagleism has genuinely evolved as:
a. Fraternalism. The fraternal “ism” in the Philippine Eagles has sprung from its declaration of policies and objectives seeking to “establish a strong bond of brotherhood and fraternities among members as keys to service.” As an offshoot, the guiding principle of the Philippine Eagles is clearly articulated, that is “Service Through Strong Brotherhood”.
b. Humanitarianism. This pertains to the ethical commitment or concern for human welfare or relations in general of Eaglemembers and shall be expressed in philanthropic activities or interest in social reforms.
c. Nationalism. This means that the Philippine Eagles “shall and give its humanitarian service, usefulness and relevance to the Philippine community and its people”; and shall pursue vigilantly and intensely its personal humanitarian service geared to give maximum benefit to the needy sectors of the Philippine community and its people.
d. Alalayang Agila. This means reliability of the Eagle-member’s commitment to fellow Eagle-members to help and come to aid if in need, exemplified in what the Philippine Eagles institutionally called the “Alalayang Agila”.
As such, Alalayang Agila pertains that Eagle-members shall have shared each others problem or moments of importance and shall have expanded and enhanced their sense and spirit of brotherhood.
This concept of Eagleism is contained in the 1989 Magna Carta of the Philippine Eagles. In this Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024, it was abbreviated for easy understanding but for ready reference the whole text of “What is Eagleism” is hereto reproduced in toto as Appendix “F”.
3

articles.summary: ARTICLE III PHILIPPINE EAGLES STRUCTURE AND GOVERNANCE CHAPTER 1 FORMATION AND NAME OF THE NATIONAL FRATERNITY
articles.content:
--- Page 32 ---
ARTICLE III
PHILIPPINE EAGLES STRUCTURE AND GOVERNANCE
CHAPTER 1
FORMATION AND NAME OF THE NATIONAL FRATERNITY
SECTION 1. Name of the National Fraternity. The Philippine Eagles formed herein shall be known and called as The Fraternal Order of Eagles - Philippine Eagles Incorporated, TFOE-PE, Inc., or briefly called Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 2. Definition of Terms. As used in this Philippine Eagles Constitution and By-Laws:
a. “The Philippine Eagles” shall refer to The Fraternal Order of Eagles-Philippine Eagles, Incorporated (TFOE-PE, Inc.).
b. “The Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024” shall refer to the Philippine Eagles Constitution of the Philippine Eagles, thoroughly reviewed in EY 2023, revised and ratified in EY 2024 .
c. “National Assembly” shall refer to the National Assembly as herein created and provided hereof.
d. “Supreme Tribunal” shall refer to the Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal, the judicial body of the Philippine Eagles, as herein created.
e. “Region” shall refer to the Eagles region organized and chartered under the provisions hereof and duly affiliated with the Philippine Eagles.
f. “Eagles Club” shall refer to the Eagles Club organized and chartered within a region and created under the provisions hereof.
g. “Eagle-Member” (irrespective of gender and number) shall refer to an individual duly affiliated to the Philippine Eagles or to any Eagles Club within a region.

--- Page 33 ---
h. “Auxiliary Member” - shall refer to a Lady Eagles and Junior Eagles as provided herein.
i.

“Board of Trustees” - shall refer to the members of the Board of Trustees of the Philippine Eagles.
CHAPTER 2
DECLARATION OF OBJECTIVES

SECTION 1. Declaration of Objectives. Among the objective of the Philippine Eagles are a) The Philippine Eagles shall extend its humanitarian service, usefulness and relevance to the Philippine society and other countries; b) To pursue vigilantly and intensely its personal humanitarian service geared to give benefit to the less privileged and marginalized sector of society.
CHAPTER 3
PHILIPPINE EAGLES CODE OF LAWS
SECTION 1. Promulgation of Philippine Eagles Code of Laws. There is hereby promulgated the Philippine Eagles Code of Laws which is hereafter set forth in Article VI of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and those to be provided and approved by the National Assembly, for the guidance and proper observance in running the affairs and governance of the Philippine Eagles.
CHAPTER 4
GOVERNANCE OF THE PHILIPPINE EAGLES
SECTION 1. The Governance in the National level. The governance of the Philippine Eagles shall be distributed among three distinct bodies, namely, the 1) The National Assembly, the 2) The Executive, and 3) The Supreme Tribunal.

--- Page 34 ---
SECTION 2. The Legislative Power. The Legislative Power shall be vested in and exercised by the National Assembly and such other inferior legislative bodies as the National Assembly may create and empower.
SECTION 3. The Executive Power. The Executive Power shall be vested in and exercised by the National President of the Philippine Eagles, and such other subordinate executive officers as may be given executive powers by the National Assembly and provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 4. The Judicial Power. The Judicial Power shall be vested in and exercised by the Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal as provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution and such other inferior Eagles grievance tribunal committees in the Region or Eagles Club, as it may deem necessary.
CHAPTER 5
THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES OF THE PHILIPPINE EAGLES
SECTION 1. The Corporate Powers. - The corporate powers of the Philippine Eagles also known as The Fraternal Order of Eagles-Philippine Eagles, Inc. (TFOE-PE,Inc.), a non-stock corporation shall be exercised by the Board of Trustees (BOT), and all business conducted and all property of the non-stock corporation shall be controlled and held by the Board of the Trustees under the name TFOE-PE,Inc.
SECTION 2. The Board of Trustees and the National Fraternity. - Unless otherwise provided by law, the Board of Trustees shall exercise the corporate powers, conduct all business, and control all properties of the Philippine Eagles. The term corporate powers shall not be understood as separate and distinct from fraternal powers. The distinction between the non-stock corporation and that of the National Fraternity must be eliminated to avoid conflict of powers and functions.

--- Page 35 ---
SECTION 3. Philippine Eagles Book of Membership. - The Board of Trustees of the Philippine Eagles including all bonafide Eagle-members must be duly registered in accordance with the existing law, rules and regulation and must be in the Roll of Eagle-members in the National Registry or Book of Membership of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 4. Powers of the National Assembly in relation to Board of Trustee. - The National Assembly remains to be the highest policy making body of the Philippine Eagles when acting collectively for and in TFOE-PE. The powers and authorities of the Board of Trustees emanate from the members of the National Assembly. Any member of the Board of Trustees may be removed by the National Assembly at any time subject to the condition that substantial and procedural requirements for the removal thereof must be strictly complied with.
SECTION 5. Election of BOT by the National Congress. - The Board of Trustees shall be composed of fifteen (15) members who shall all be elected by the members through their delegates in the National Congress, namely: the regional governors, vice-governors and three (3)
national assemblymen or alternate national assemblymen; in case of the absence of the national assemblymen and the ex-officio members of the National Assembly or National Congress. In the TFOE-PE, Inc., the national election, which shall be held annually on the last day of the two-day annual National Congress shall generally be held in the 3rd Saturday and Sunday of November unless there is a force majeure; and in accordance with the Philippine Eagles Constitution and to the corresponding rules to be issued by the Philippine Eagles Elections Commission (PhiEleCom) pursuant to Article VII hereof and other relevant provisions on this Constitution on elective positions.
SECTION 6. All Candidates for BOT as Members of the National Assembly. - All candidates for the position of Board of Trustees must submit their Certificates of Candidacy to the Nomination Committee of the (PhiEleCom) of the Philippine Eagles within thirty (30) days prior

--- Page 36 ---
to the day of the national election, for qualification and evaluation.
Any candidate running for the BOT must either be member of the National Assembly as a Regional Governor, Vice Governor or National Assemblyman and must be a member of the Philippine Eagles for at least three (3) years and of the National Assembly for at least two Eagle Years.
SECTION 7. List of Qualified Candidates. - The list of qualified and eligible candidates for the positions of Board of Trustees, shall be published by PhiEleCom En Banc in the social media, Facebook Pages and/or other digital publication fora of the Philippine Eagles not later than seven (7) days prior to the day of the national election.
SECTION 8. Term of Office. - The term of office of the duly elected Board of Trustees shall be for two (2) years and shall begin on the first day of January preceding the election and end on the last day of December two Eagle Years after following their election.
SECTION 9. Composition, Election and Term of Trustees. – The Board of Trustees shall be composed of fifteen (15) members: a) five (5)
members representing the Executive namely: National President (NP), Executive National Vice President (ENVP), Vice President for Luzon, (VPL), Vice President for Visayas (VPV), and Vice President for Mindanao VPM; b) one Past President (1) and a member of PENAPLE and; c) nine (9) members representing the National Assembly. The number of Board of Trustees as provided herein shall be fixed in the Articles of Incorporation and By-laws. The Board of Trustees shall have a term of two (2) years and as such, they shall hold office for not more than two (2) years until their successors are elected and qualified.
Trustees elected to fill vacancies occurring before the expiration of a particular term shall hold office for the unexpired period.
In the election of the Board of Trustees, the majority of the members of the National Assembly entitled and qualified to vote must be present, but all members of the National Assembly must be duly

--- Page 37 ---
notified at least one (1) month prior to said election either manually or electronically.
Duly affiliated Eagles Regions in overseas or other countries shall be entitled to vote through absentee voting or other mechanism based on the rules to be promulgated by Philippine Eagles Elections Commission (PhiEleCom) and subject to the approval of the National Assembly.
SECTION 10. Representation, Authority, Responsibility and Governance.
– Duly elected members of the Board of Trustees shall be the representative of TFOE-PE, Inc. in dealing with juridical persons or entities. The Board of Trustee shall:
a. Be responsible for any act or omission that binds the Philippine Eagles as provided by law;
b. Assume the responsibility that carries with it the essential power to govern all the affairs of the Philippine Eagles in harmony with the National Assembly and the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024;
c. Observe the resolutions approved by the National Assembly and by the Board of Trustees that must be respected by both bodies pursuant to the concept of good governance;
d. Enforce limitation, restriction and conditions contained in this Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024 and the By-Laws;
e. Have overall responsibility of the management of the corporate affairs of the Fraternal Order of Eagles-Philippine Eagles, Inc. The Board of Trustees typically the governing body of the non-stock corporation and seek to ensure the best of interest of the members in all types of management decision; f.

Monitor the Philippine Eagles adherence to all laws and regulations and adopt policies and procedure to and legal ethical standards that guide every aspect of the TFOE-PE, Inc.
for effective governance; and

--- Page 38 ---
g. Ensure compliance with laws and regulations, oversee the Philippine Eagles’ goals and purposes and represent Eaglemember stakeholders such as donors and beneficiaries.
SECTION 11. Manner of the Elections of the Board of Trustees. - The fifteen (15) members of the Board of Trustees shall be elected by the duly qualified members of the National Congress as follows:
a. The National President (NP), Executive National VicePresident (ENVP) and 1 Past President from PENAPLE shall be elected at large and the candidate receiving the highest number of votes for each said position shall be elected NP, ENVP and a member of BOT representing the PENAPLE, respectively.
b. The Vice President for Luzon (VPL), Vice President for Visayas (VPV) and Vice-President for Mindanao (VPM), in order to provide representation in each geographical location and not to interfere in the affairs of regional aggrupation in Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, only qualified delegates from Luzon Regions shall elect the VPL; only qualified delegates from Visayas Regions shall elect the VPV; and only qualified each from Mindanao Regions shall elect the VPM. The candidate receiving the highest number of votes for said positions shall be declared elected VPL, VPV and VPM, respectively.
c. The nine (9) members of the Board of Trustees shall be elected at large based on the following geographical representation:
i) four (4) shall be elected from Luzon Regions ii) three (3)
from Mindanao Regions and iii) two (2) from Visayas Regions.
d. Four (4) candidates from Luzon receiving the four highest numbers of votes shall be declared elected members of BOT representing Luzon; Three (3) candidates from Mindanao receiving the three (3) highest number of votes shall be declared elected members of BOT: and two (2) candidates from Visayas receiving the two (2) highest number of votes shall be declared members of BOT, respectively.

--- Page 39 ---
SECTION 12. The Other Corporate Officers. – After the National Congress election, the Board of Trustees, shall formally organize and elect the following:
a. Corporate Treasurer, who must be an Eagle member, resident and citizen of the Philippines;
b. Corporate Secretary, an Eagle member who must be a citizen and resident of the Philippines;
c. Such other officers as may be provided in the By-Laws.
The same person may hold two (2) or more positions concurrently, except that no one shall act as President and Secretary or as President and Treasurer at the same time, unless otherwise allowed by law. The officers shall manage the non-stock corporation and perform such duties as may be provided in the By-laws and/or as resolved by the Board of Trustees.
SECTION 13. Ex-Officio Members of the Board of Trustees. - Consistent with the provisions of RA No.11232, otherwise known as the Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines, there is hereby created ExOfficio Members of the Board of Trustees composed of seven (7)
members, namely, five (5) from the PENAPLE and two (2) from PEIL.
The representatives of PEIL will be the Executive PEIL Director (EPD)
and the Senior PEIL Director (SPD). In case there is no SPD or inability of the SPD to attend, the EPD shall elect among the PEIL Directors who shall represent the PEIL in the BOT.
All Ex-Officio members of the BOT are entitled to all rights and privileges accorded to BOT except the right to vote.
SECTION 14. Per Diem of the BOT. - The Board of Trustees shall not receive any compensation, except for reasonable per diems.
Reasonable per diems may be granted to Trustees by the vote of the members representing at least a majority of the membership at a regular or special members’ meeting called for the purpose. In

--- Page 40 ---
no case shall the total yearly compensation Board of Trustees must not exceed 15% (percent) of the net income before income tax of the non-stock corporation during the preceding year as required by law and shall be subject to usual accounting and auditing rules:
Provided, That, the percentage as required by law on the total yearly compensation of Board of Trustees may be decreased based on the National Assembly Act to be sponsored by the Chairman of the Finance and Appropriations Committee taking into consideration historical expenses of the Board of Trustees per year, needs and subject to the availability of funds.
SECTION 15. Proper Observance and Compliance of RA No. 11232 and SEC Issuances. - The Board of Trustees shall properly observe and comply with the provisions of RA No. 11232 otherwise known as the Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines, relative to the provisions on non-stock corporation including all SEC related rules and regulations and issuances thereto.
CHAPTER 6
PHILIPPINE EAGLES REGIONS AND EAGLES CLUBS
SECTION 1. Rules on the Establishment, Chartering and Apportionment of Eagles Club and Eagles Region. In order to achieve the goals and objectives as well as the purposes of the Philippine Eagles, Eagles clubs, regions shall be established, chartered and apportioned in accordance with Article IX of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
CHAPTER 7
FOUNDING YEAR AND PHILIPPINE EAGLES WEEK
SECTION 1. Recognition of the By-Laws in 1979. The Declaration of Goals and Objectives of The Fraternal Order of Eagles-Philippine Eagle, Inc. which was ratified and adopted on 28 June 1979 at the U.P.
Asian Institute of Tourism in Quezon City, Philippines, are hereby

--- Page 41 ---
recognized, it shall form part and be an integral part of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and corresponding rules and acts of the Philippine Eagles, as promulgated.
SECTION 2. The Philippine Eagles Foundation Day. The Philippine Eagles shall celebrate annually its Founding Anniversary on June 22 which shall be officially known and called the Philippine Eagles Foundation Day.
SECTION 3. The Philippine Eagles Week.
A. In conformity with and pursuant to Proclamation No.
600, S. 1995, Office of the President of the Republic of the Philippines, every year from June 15 to 22, is officially known as The Philippine Eagles Week.
B. Programs, activities and projects nationwide shall be under the directive of the National President. All activities, programs and projects in Eagles Club and Regions shall be aligned with and that of the National President based on his directives.

articles.title: Bill of Rights and Obligations of Eagle Members
articles.summary: ARTICLE IV BILL OF RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF EAGLE-MEMBERS CHAPTER 1 RIGHTS OF EAGLE-MEMBERS
articles.content:
--- Page 42 ---
ARTICLE IV
BILL OF RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF EAGLE-MEMBERS
CHAPTER 1
RIGHTS OF EAGLE-MEMBERS
SECTION 1. Equal Rights and Privileges. Chartered Eagles Regions and Eagles Clubs in good standing shall enjoy equal rights and privileges under this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 2. Right to Fraternal Membership. Membership to any duly chartered Eagles Club shall be protected, subject to certain limitations.
Such membership, although voluntary, shall be fraternal.
SECTION 3. Right to Affiliation. Every Eagle-member shall have the right to choose his club affiliation subject to the provisions on Sections and Article on Membership hereof.
SECTION 4. Right to Freely Express Opinion. Every Eagle-member shall freely and openly express his views and opinions in courteous manner but his divergent views and opinions shall always yield to the view of the majority of the members in proper forum or venue.
SECTION 5. Right to be Elected or Appointed. Every Eagle-member has the right to serve in any level of governance in Philippine Eagles whether elective or appointive shall be granted and held inviolable in application of the constitutional guarantee of equal protection clause. All Eagle-members in the Philippine Eagles shall henceforth be considered of the same class and of the same general standing4.
SECTION 6. Right Against Discrimination. Every Eagle-member has the right to be treated equally, regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, color, rank or title and discrimination is strictly prohibited.
4

Eagle Membership Reform Act of 2009

--- Page 43 ---
SECTION 7. Right to Freedom of Expression. Every Eagle-member has the right to express his opinion, idea and concern constructively within his Eagles Club, region or Philippine Eagles in a courteous manner.
SECTION 8. Right to Freedom of Information. Every Eagle-member has the right to access organizational documents, financial reports and minutes of the meetings of the National Assembly, National Congress, and Board of Trustees for transparency and accountability.
SECTION 9. Right to Participation. Every Eagle-member in good standing has the right to participate in organizational activities, events, meetings and programs.
SECTION 10. Right against Retaliaton. Every Eagle-member reporting misconduct, malfeasance or misfeasance of any Eagle-member or participating in investigation thereof has the right to be protected from retaliation.
SECTION 11. Right to Due Process. Every Eagle-member accused of violating organizational rules, National Assembly Acts and adopted Resolutions shall have the right to due process such as impartial and fair hearing, present evidence in his behalf and submit controverting evidence and present witnesses.
SECTION 12. Right to Appeal. Every Eagle-member has the right to appeal any decision affecting his membership status such as suspension or expulsion, as the case may be, by an impartial body, and within a specified period of time.
SECTION 13. Right to Data Privacy. Every Eagle-member has the right to confidentiality of information as guaranteed under RA No. 10173 - Data Privacy Act. Personal information about any Eagle-member shall be kept confidential and may be used only for legitimate organizational purpose. The right to privacy of Eagle-member extends to communication, membership records and financial matters.

--- Page 44 ---
SECTION 14. Right to Safety Environment. Every Eagle-member has the right to a safe and respectful organizational environment and prohibit strictly harassment, hazing, other harmful behaviors and profane languages and abuse.
CHAPTER 2
OBLIGATIONS OF EAGLE-MEMBERS
SECTION 1. Obligation to Obey the Constitution and Laws. Every Eagle-member shall defend and uphold at all times the Philippine Eagles Constitution, as well as all laws rules and regulations duly promulgated by the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 2. Eagles Delicadeza and Moral Code of Ethics. Every Eaglemember shall consciously uphold at all times the Eagles Delicadeza and Moral Code of Ethics as the ultimate measure of his conduct and judgment relative to his dealings with the Philippine Eagles Region, Eagles Club and with fellow Eagle-member.
SECTION 3. Obligation to Keep Membership in Good Standing. Every Eagle-Member shall have the obligation to keep his membership always in good standing.
SECTION 4. Obligation to Undertake Community Outreach and Humanitarian Service. Every Eagles Club shall be committed to undertake annually at least four (4) community outreach or humanitarian service that shall be beneficial to the community in need, in particular, and our country, in general or even in the other countries or overseas.
SECTION 5. Obligation to Help Fellow Eagle-Member. Every Eaglemember shall be fraternally committed to help his brother fellow Eagle-member as exemplified in what the Philippine Eagles called “Alalayang Agila”.

--- Page 45 ---
SECTION 6. Obligation to Adhere to Eagles Club and Region. Every Eagle-member shall develop a strong faith and belief and adherence to his club or region and to the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 7. Obligation to Avoid Conflict. As a fraternal organization, no conflict or difference shall remain permanent among Eagle-member Eagles club or region and the Philippine Eagle. Every Eagle-member shall strive to adhere to this positive thinking and belief to avoid conflict or differences.
SECTION 8. Obligation to Observe Proper Conduct in Social Media.
Every Eagle-member is prohibited in exchanging or posting through social media unpleasant and unnecessary comment/s that might tarnish the reputation or good name of any Eagle-member, Eagles Club, region, national officers and the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 9. Obligation to Observe Mutual Respect and Good Manners.
Every Eagle-member shall show mutual respect to his fellow Eaglemember and must act and relate in good manner.
SECTION 10. Obligation to Plant Trees. As the institutional policy of the Philippine Eagles, it is mandatory for all Eagle-member of Eagles Club and Region to undertake a continuing and sustainable tree planting program which may be applicable in the areas of their concern where the Eagles Clubs or Eagles Region are located or it may deem necessary, where tree planting and growing are needed.
If applicable, a Region or Eagles Club may adopt a mountain for its tree planting and growing program.
The Eagles Clubs and Regions shall submit accordingly their quarterly reports on their tree-planting and growing program as they may have undertaken to the Secretary General. (The Philippine Eagles Planting Program of 1994)
SECTION 11. Obligation to Pay Dues. Every Eagle-member is obliged to

--- Page 46 ---
pay his annual dues and other financial obligations as authorized and determined by the National, Regional and Eagles Club as well as other affiliation fees and institutional assessment as may be promulgated by the Philippine Eagles. (Pursuant to Club Dues Act of 1994)
SECTION 12. Obligation to Follow Laws Faithfully. Every Eagle-member is obliged to follow all laws, rules and regulations duly promulgated by the Philippine Eagles and that of the National Assembly in complete adherence to the words that an Eagle-member is a law-abiding citizen.
As such, among others, the Philippine Eagles uphold and observe strictly the implementation of RA No. 8049 otherwise known as the Anti-Hazing Law; RA 7877, titled Anti-Sexual Harassment Act; and RA 11313 also known as the Safe Spaces Act or Bawal Bastos Law.
SECTION 13. Obligation to Renew His Membership on Time. Every Eaglemember is obliged to maintain his membership in good standing and must renew his membership annualy, preferably at the 1st Quarter of calendar year.

ARTICLE V
GOVERNANCE OF THE PHILIPPINE EAGLES
SECTION 1. Distribution of Governance. The governance of the Philippine Eagles shall be distributed among three distinct bodies, namely, the National Assembly, the Executive and the Supreme Tribunal.
SECTION 2. The Legislative Power. The Legislative power shall be vested in and exercised by the National Assembly and such other legislative bodies as the National Assembly may create and empower, such as Regional Assembly and Club General Membership.
SECTION 3. The Executive Power. The Executive power shall be vested in and exercised by the National President of the Philippine Eagles, and such other National executive officers as may be given executive powers by the National Assembly and provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 4. The Judicial Power. The Judicial power shall be vested in and exercised by the Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal as provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution and such other Eagles grievance tribunal committees in the Region or Eagles Club, as it may deem necessary.

articles.content:
--- Page 48 ---
ARTICLE VI
PHILIPPINE EAGLES CODE OF LAWS
CHAPTER 1
TITLE AND APPLICABILITY
SECTION 1. Title. This Article shall be known and cited as the Philippine Eagles Code of Laws of The Fraternal Order of Eagles–Philippines Eagles, Inc. or for brevity Philippine Eagles Code of Laws.
SECTION 2. Applicability. This Article shall apply to all matters relating to the organization, administrative, legislative and judicial authorities, powers, and general administration of The Fraternal Order of EaglesPhilippine Eagles, Inc. including all Eagles Regions and Clubs duly chartered and affiliated to the Philippine Eagles.
CHAPTER 2
DEFINITIONS AND IDENTIFICATIONS
SECTION 1. As used in this Article provisions of the Eagles Constitution.
A. “Philippine Eagles” shall refer to The Fraternal Order of Eagles- Philippine Eagles, Inc., or National Fraternity.
B. “Philippine Eagles Constitution” or shall refer to the Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024.
C. “National Act,” or “National Resolution” which may be interchangeably used, shall refer to all measures passed and approved by the National Assembly.
D. “National Assembly” which may be abbreviated as Assembly shall refer to the National Assembly of the Philippine Eagles.
E. “Regional Governor” shall refer to the incumbent or charter Regional Governor of the duly affiliated Region and member

--- Page 49 ---
of the National Assembly of the Philippine Eagles.
F. “Appointments Commission (APCOM)” shall refer to the Philippine Eagles Appointments Commission created hereafter.
G. “Executive Officers” shall refer to the presidential appointees under the Executive body, duly appointed by the National President.
H. “Eagles Club” shall refer to any Eagles Club duly chartered and affiliated with the Philippine Eagles.
I.

“Supreme Tribunal” shall refer to the Supreme Tribunal of the Philippine Eagles.

J.

“Bonafide member” shall be an Eagle-Member who is in good standing and whose Region and Club is also in good standing, duly affiliated with the Philippine Eagles as listed in Roll of Eagles of the TFOE-PE, Inc. or in the Book of Membership.
CHAPTER 3
DISTRIBUTION OF POWERS

SECTION 1. Triad of Powers. The Governance of the Philippine Eagles shall be distributed among three distinct Bodies, namely the Legislative, Executive and Judiciary.
SECTION 2. Legislative Powers. The Legislative powers shall be vested in and exercised by the National Assembly, Regional Assembly or Club General Membership meeting, as the case maybe: Provided, That only matters affecting the interest of the Region or Eagles Club may be passed or adopted by said Region or Eagles Club, as the case may be: Provided, Finally that on matters affecting the Philippine Eagles as a whole, only the National Assembly shall pass and adopt the appropriate measures.

--- Page 50 ---
SECTION 3. Executive Powers. The Executive powers shall be vested in and exercised by the National President of the Philippine Eagles, the Regional Governors, and Eagles Club Presidents, as the case may be.
SECTION 4. Judicial Powers. The Judicial powers shall be vested in and exercised by the Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal as created in this Philippine Eagles Constitution and such other grievance tribunal committee created or established in the Region or Eagles Club, as necessary.
CHAPTER 4
THE LEGISLATIVE
SECTION 1. National Assembly Composition. The National Assembly shall be composed of the duly elected National Officers, Ex-Officio Members, Regional Governors, Vice Governors, National Assemblymen or Alternate National Assemblymen. All of them shall be called members of the National Assembly.
The ex-officio members of the National Assembly who shall have the voting rights shall be the following:
a. All members of the PENAPLE, as provided in Article XIV;
b. The Secretary General;
c. The Executive Director of the Philippines Eagles Institute of Leadership (Omnibus Amendment of 2008);
d. The Attorney General;
e. The Chief Legal Counsel for Fraternal Affairs; f.

National Treasurer; and

g. The Auditor General.
SECTION 2. National Assembly Powers, Duties and Functions. The National Assembly shall be the highest law-making and policymaking

--- Page 51 ---
body of the Philippine Eagles. It shall further exercise all powers, authorities and functions of the Philippine Eagles which are not otherwise expressly or clearly provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 3. National Assembly Officers. The Officers of the National Assembly shall be the Presiding Officer, the Floor Leader, the National Assembly Secretary, and the Sergeant-at-Arms whose powers, duties and functions shall be set by the National Assembly.
SECTION 4. National Assembly Standing Committees. The National Assembly shall have the following standing committees:
a. Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee;
b. Membership Committee;
c. Good Governance and Investigation Committee;
d. Judiciary, Revision of Codes and Acts Committee;
e. Finance and Appropriations Committee; and f.

Such other Committee as may deem necessary for the furtherance of the goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles.

The powers, duties and functions of the standing committees shall be governed by Rule VI, Rules of the National Assembly, Article VIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 5. Appointments Commission Composition.
a. There shall be an Appointments Commission (APCOM)
composed of a Chairman, Vice-Chairman headed by a member of PENAPLE and BOT and three (3) elected members of the National Assembly chosen based on equal geographical representation, preferably representing all geographical regions of the Philippine Eagles, who shall be chosen among the duly recognized delegates of the National

--- Page 52 ---
Assembly at the annual National Congress in the 3rd week of November.
b. Upon their proclamation by the Philippine Eagles Elections Commission (PhiEleCom) during the National Congress, the three (3) Elected APCOM members shall perform their duties and powers.
SECTION 6. APCOM Action on Appointments. APCOM shall act on the appointments submitted to Commission by the National President within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the submission. The action or decision on the appointments may be decided at by a consensus vote of the majority of its members to be secured by the Chairman before acting on appointments.
SECTION 7. APCOM Powers, Duties and Functions. The APCOM shall have the power to approve or disapprove appointments by the National President based on merits and qualifications.
The APCOM shall return to the National President the appointment submitted to it by the latter which it shall either approve or disapprove.
If disapproved, it shall briefly state its reason for disapproving the appointment.
The National President shall not reappoint to the same national position the appointee whose appointment thereto shall have been disapproved by the APCOM; SECTION 8. APCOM Term of Office. The term of office of the Chairman and Members of the Commission shall be for two (2) years. In Case of vacancy, there shall be an election to fill-up the vacant position.
CHAPTER 5
THE EXECUTIVE
SECTION 1. Chief Executive and his Cabinet. The National President shall be the Chief Executive of the Philippine Eagles. His executive

--- Page 53 ---
officers shall be the following: The Secretary General, Attorney General, Chief Legal Counsel for Fraternal Affairs, Information Secretary, Finance Secretary, National Treasurer, Property Custodian, and the Executive Director of the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership and such other national officers whose appointments may be vested upon him by this Philippine Eagles Constitution or authorized and created by the National Assembly.
SECTION 2. Term of Office of the National President. The National President shall serve for two (2) years without re-election. Eagle National President who has served for at least two (2) years shall not be eligible to run again for the position of National President.
SECTION 3. Powers of the National President. The National President shall:
a. Be the presiding officer of the National Assembly and shall automatically become the President of the Board of Trustees;
b. Appoint the executive officers, including but not limited to, the Secretary General, Attorney General, Chief Legal Counsel for Fraternal Affairs, Information Secretary, Finance Secretary, National Treasurer, Property Custodian, Directors of the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL), Editor/s of the Philippine Eagles Forum and such other officers whose appointments are now or hereafter shall be vested in the National President, including the power to remove said appointees.
c. Represent the Philippine Eagles in all of its official functions;
d. Conduct regular Region or Eagles Club visitations and dialogue; and
e. Exercise such other powers, duties and functions as the Philippine Eagles Charter or statutes may now or hereafter provide and such as are inherent or incidental to his office or position.

--- Page 54 ---
SECTION 4. Additional Powers, Duties and Functions of National President (NP). As Chief Executive of the Philippine Eagles, the National President is vested with the following power, duties, and functions:
a. To preside at the meeting of the Board of Trustee and the Executive;
b. To act as Ex-officio member of the Philippine Eagles National Presidents’ League (PENAPLE) during his term of office;
c. To address the Philippine Eagles National Assembly and deliver his state of Eagleism address at its first regular session or he may deem necessary;
d. To see to it that the agenda of the session of the National Assembly shall be properly prepared and disseminated by the National Assembly’s Secretary to the members of the National Assembly and the ex-officio members at least one
(1) month prior to the session observing and following the order of business under Rule XI, Article VIII, Rules of the National Assembly of this Philippine Eagles Constitution;
e. To ensure the dignity and solemnity of the proceedings of the National Assembly and punctual attendance of the members during the session as required.
f.

If feasible, to address at least once during his term, the regional assembly of each Eagles region which shall be simultaneous with his visitorial dialogue with the Eagles Clubs in the region;

g. To enhance, at all times the stature and prestige of the presidency of the Philippine Eagles;
h. As the rallying figure of the Philippines Eagles, to keep, evolve and secure the position of a National President; as distinguished position of trust and special privilege; and i.

30

To appoint other Executive Officers, the Supreme Chancellor and Associate Chancellors of the Supreme Tribunal, the

--- Page 55 ---
Chairman and Commissioners of the PhiEleCom and other national officers whose appointments may have been vested in him by the Philippine Eagles Constitution or by the Eagles Laws and submit their appointments to the Philippine Eagles APCOM for appropriate action not later than January 15 following their official assumptions into office in accordance with the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 5. Powers of Executive National Vice President (ENVP). The Executive National Vice President (ENVP) shall be elected among the duly elected Regional governors simultaneously with the National President on the last day of the annual National Congress which shall generally be held in the 3rd week of November unless there is force majeure. He shall:
a. Become the National President in case of death or permanent disability or incapacity of the incumbent National President to perform the powers and discharge the duties and functions of the presidency for the remainder of the term vacated;
b. Be acting as National President in the event that the National President shall have left the Philippines, except on official functions;
c. Be acting as National President in case of temporary disability or incapacity of the National President; and
d. Preside at the National Assembly session in the event the National President shall yield the Chair to enable the latter to participate in the discussion or deliberation of the National Assembly.
SECTION 6. Powers, Duties and Functions of National Vice President.
The National Vice President elected geographically shall:
a. Be the Chief Executive of his region and shall automatically be the Chairman of aggrupation of Regional Governors within his geographical jurisdiction;

--- Page 56 ---
b. Preside over the sessions or meeting of the aggrupation of Regional Governors, within his geographical jurisdiction;
c. In the absence of the National President, represent the National President in all official functions of the Philippine Eagles and Eagles Regions and Clubs held in his region, as authorized and within his geographical jurisdiction;
d. Exercise such powers, duties and functions as are now or hereafter shall be vested in him by this Philippine Eagles Constitution; and
e. Perform such powers and discharge such other duties and functions as the National President or the National Assembly may require him to do.
SECTION 7. Powers and Duties of Secretary General. The Secretary General shall:
a. Be the Chief Administrative Ofiicer of the Philippine Eagles;
b. Exercise general supervision over the National Secretariat;
c. With the written authority of the National President, appoint the personnel of the National Secretariat as may be deemed necessary;
d. Coordinate and monitor the activities of the Eagles Regions and Eagles Clubs;
e. Attend and monitor the National Assembly and National Congress as an ex-officio member; (as amended by 2008 omnibus amendments)
f.

For proper coordination, submit to PEIL the schedule of MANDATES; and

g. Perform such powers and discharge such other duties and functions as the National President or the National Assembly may require him to do from time to time.

--- Page 57 ---
SECTION 8. Qualifications and Removal of the Secretary General. The qualifications for appointment and the removal from Office of the Secretary General are hereto provided:
a. No Eagle-member may be appointed to the position of Secretary General unless he is a member in good standing of any Eagles Club which must equally be an Eagles Club in good standing for at least two (2) years preceding his appointment;
b. Aside from good standing, no Eagle-member may be appointed to the position of the Secretary General unless he has completed the day long Leadership Seminar (LEADS)
prescribed by the Philippine Institute of Leadership (PEIL)
and shall has served either as Executive National Vice President, Regional Governor, or National Assemblyman of the Philippine Eagles, or Director of the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL); and
c. The Secretary General duly appointed may only be removed by the National President after due process for abuse of powers, inefficiency or misfeasance or malfeasance in office.
(Omnibus Amendment of 2005)
SECTION 9. Powers and Duties of Attorney General. The Attorney General shall be the public defender of The Fraternal Order of EaglesPhilippine Eagles, Inc. and all its institutions, in any internal dispute, conflict, controversy or problem which may affect or involve the Philippine Eagles. He shall:
a. Defend, uphold and maintain at all times the Philippine Eagles Constitution, its duly promulgated laws, statutes, rules and regulations or adopted resolutions or acts of the National Assembly, and by the Board of Trustees;
b. Defend, uphold and maintain and apply at all times the Philippine Eagles Delicadeza and Moral Code of Ethics, as the

--- Page 58 ---
ultimate basis of his conduct and judgment toward resolving any internal dispute, conflict or controversy in the Philippine Eagles, Regions, Clubs, or the Eagle-members in general;
c. Defend, uphold and maintain at all times the institutional tenets, creed and goals or the Philippine Eagles wherever and whenever called upon to do so;
d. Appear before the Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal in such cases and matters brought before the said Tribunal as the official advocate of the Philippine Eagles and where a definitive stand shall be necessary, to uphold and defend the Philippine Eagles Constitution, its institutional tenets, creed and goals, that he shall be duty bound to do so;
e. In proper time and cases, be the head of the Philippine Eagles free legal aid which shall be pursued under his initiative in line with the humanitarian ends of the Philippine Eagles; and f.

Exercise such legal powers and discharge such other duties and functions inherent, traditional or peculiar to the office of the Attorney General.

SECTION 10. Powers and Duties of Chief Legal Counsel for Fraternal Affairs. The Legal Counsel for Fraternal Affairs shall:
a. Provide legal advice to the National President in dealing with affiliated Regions, Eagles Clubs, and Eagles-members;
b. Review contracts and documents submitted and forwarded by the Philippine Eagles Commissions, Special Commissions, Board of Trustees and other bodies in the Executive.
c. Advice the National President on the pending National Assembly bills and resolutions and recommend to the Executive the priority measures needed by the Philippine Eagles;
d. Render counsel to the Executive on the proper implementation and observance of the provisions of the Philippine Eagles Constitution; and

--- Page 59 ---
e. Exercise such legal powers and discharge such other duties and functions inherent, or peculiar to the office of a Legal Counsel of a non-stock corporation.
SECTION 11. Powers and Duties of Information Secretary. The Information Secretary shall:
a. Have charge and direction of the Eagles publicity about the Philippine Eagles, Eagles Regions and Club;
b. With the approval of the National President, issue statements regarding the Philippine Eagles its activities, programs, and projects;
c. Monitor and collate activities of the Philippine Eagles, regions and clubs for dissemination to the tri-media; and other communication pages online; and
d. Perform such powers and discharge such other duties and functions as the National President or the National Assembly may require him to do from time to time.
SECTION 12. Powers and Duties of Finance Secretary. The Finance Secretary shall:
a. Be the Chairman of the Finance and Appropriations Committee which shall prepare the annual budget of the Philippine Eagles, in consultation with the BOT, and subject to the confirmation of the National Assembly;
b. Devise ways and means to raise funds and revenues for the Philippine Eagles or in the name of TFOE-PE, Inc.; and
c. Perform such powers and discharge such other duties and functions as the National President or the National Assembly may require him to do from time to time.
SECTION 13. Powers and Duties of National Treasurer. The National Treasurer shall have the custody of all funds and properties of the Philippine Eagles and shall exercise the following powers and duties.

--- Page 60 ---
a. Subject to the counter sign-signature of the National President, or such other officer as may be designated by the Board of Trustees shall sign all checks, drafts, notes or order of payment of money or withdrawal of funds of the Philippine Eagles;
b. He shall endorse for deposit to the credit of the Philippine Eagles, with such banks and financial institution as may be designated by the Board of Trustees;
c. Keep and maintain the financial accounts of the Philippine Eagles; collect and deposit all moneys received by the Philippine Eagles or in the name of TFOE-PE, Inc, and issue receipts therefore;
d. Prepare financial statements quarterly and render detailed financial report to the National Assembly with physical copy or via electronic means at least one week before the National Assembly;
e. Shall render an annual statement of assets and liabilities of the Philippine Eagles for the approval of the Board of Trustees, and a statement of the cash account at, any time that he may be required to render by the National President; f.

Shall keep the required and proper books of account, and enter therein a full and accurate of all the moneys and properties received and paid by him in behalf of or the account of the Philippine Eagles;

g. Disburse, with the approval of the Board of Trustees and the National President, such moneys or funds necessary or incidental to the financial operations of the Philippine Eagles;
h. Disburse the funds and appropriations allocated and approved by the National Assembly; and i.

36

Perform such powers and discharge such other duties and functions as the National President may require him to do and as inherent or incidental to his position or office.

--- Page 61 ---
SECTION 14. Powers and Duties of Auditor General. The duties and functions of the Auditor General shall be as defined in Article XII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 15. Powers and Duties of Property Custodian.
a. The Property Custodian shall safeguard the properties of the Philippine Eagles and shall make inventory of all the properties acquired and owned by the Philippine Eagles in the name of TFOE-PE, Inc.,
b. Prepare a report of all properties of the Philippine Eagles semestrally and submit the same to the National Assembly; and
c. He shall have such other duties and functions as may be inherent and incidental to his office or position.
SECTION 16. Chief National Protocol Officer. The Chief National Protocol Officer shall be the highest protocol officer in the Philippine Eagles and shall see to it that the official protocol be faithfully observed during official and formal functions of the Philippine Eagles. He shall carry out and adhere to the protocol matters and observe properly the implementation of the Protocol Manuals.
CHAPTER 6
THE JUDICIARY BODY
SECTION 1. Judicial Body. The judicial power in the Philippine Eagles shall be vested in and exercised by the Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal created by this Philippine Eagles Constitution and such other grievance tribunal committee as may be created or established in the Region or Eagles Club, as it may deem necessary.
SECTION 2. Composition. The Supreme Tribunal shall be composed of one (1) Supreme Chancellor, one (1) Senior Associate Chancellor,

--- Page 62 ---
and nine (9) Associate Chancellors who shall be appointed by the National President and whose appointments shall be confirmed by the Philippine Eagles Appointments Commission. The Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal shall be divided in three (3) divisions of 4, 4, and 3 members each to efficiently handle and dispose cases submitted to the Supreme Tribunal. Each division shall handle the case referred to it subject to the appeal procedures of the Supreme Tribunal, En Banc, within 30 days from the decision of a Division.
SECTION 3. Appointments of 9 Associate Chancellors. The National President shall appoint the nine (9) Associate Chancellors and must see that out of the total nine (9) Associate Chancellors three (3) each shall come from Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao Regions.
SECTION 4. Qualifications of Supreme Chancellor, Senior Associate Chancellor and Associate Chancellors. The National President shall appoint the Supreme Chancellor, Senior Associate Chancellor and Associate Chancellors from among Eagle-members with the following qualifications:
a. Eagle-member in good standing for at least three (3) years;
b. Must have experience in the settlement of disputes as former member of the Lupon Tagapayapa in Barangay or must have knowledge and experience in conciliation, mediation or arbitration;
c. Majority of the members of Supreme Tribunal must at least be graduate of Juris Doctor or preferably lawyer; and
d. Must have proven integrity, independence, and impartiality; Provided, That, the Supreme Chancellor must be a lawyer.
SECTION 5. Powers, Duties, Functions.
The Supreme Tribunal shall:
a. Be the supreme arbiter of all internal problems and controversies brought to it on appeal by the Philippine Eagles, Region, Eagles Clubs or Eagle-Members;

--- Page 63 ---
b. Hear and decide all election contests or appeal affecting the National President, Executive National Vice President, National Vice Presidents, BOT, Regional governors and members of the National Assembly;
c. Hear and decide on appeal all cases affecting the internal problems and controversies of Eagles Region or Eagles Clubs duly affiliated to the Philippine Eagles or their eaglemembers elevated on appeal, as the case maybe;
d. Review the decision of the PhiEleCom brought to it on appeal in an election contest;
e. Convene during the National Congress and hear and decide urgent election matters that may be brought to it and be resolved peremptorily; and f.

In general, hear and decide all cases brought to the Supreme Tribunal for consideration by the Philippine Eagles, its officers, region, and Eagles club affiliates and Eagle-members.

SECTION 6. Original and Appellate Jurisdiction. The Philippine Eagles Supreme Tribunal shall decide all cases originally filed with it within thirty (30) days from the filing thereof, without extension.
SECTION 7. Term of Office. Unless the Supreme Chancellor, Senior Associate Chacellor or Associate Chancellors shall have resigned or shall have ceased to qualify, as a bonafide Eagle-member of the Philippine Eagle and duly affiliated with active Eagles club as an Eagle-member, their term of office are as follows: Four (4) years for Supreme Chancellor and Senior Chancellor, and three (3) years for Associate Chancellor.

--- Page 64 ---
CHAPTER 7
PHILIPPINE EAGLES COMMISSIONS AND SPECIAL EAGLES
COMMISSIONS AND DAKILANG BULWAGAN NG AGILA
SECTION 1. Philippine Eagles Commissions and Special Eagles Commissions
A. Philippine Eagles Commissions. The Philippine Commissions created and established in this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be governed by Chapter One, Article XI hereof:
B. Special Eagle Commissions. The Special Eagles Commissions created and established in this Eagles Constitution shall be governed by Chapter Two, Article XI hereof.
SECTION 2. Dakilang Bulwagan ng Agila. There shall be a place in the Philippine Eagles which shall be called the Dakilang Bulwagan ng Agila which is synonymous to the Hall of Fame, which shall be placed in Philippine Eagles offices.
Any Eagle-member who shall have received or shall have been awarded at least five (5) outstanding awards as catalogued in Article XI of this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be placed in the Dakilang Bulwagan ng Agila.
CHAPTER 8
EAGLES OFFICE OF TRUST AND SPECIAL PRIVILEGE
SECTION 1. Office of Trust and Special Privilege. The position in the Philippine Eagles or affiliated Regions or Eagles Clubs, whether elective or appointive, shall be an Office of Trust and a special privilege.
CHAPTER 9
MEMBERSHIP
SECTION 1. Membership by Eagles Club. Membership to the Philippine Eagles shall be by Eagles Club affiliation and shall be governed by

--- Page 65 ---
Chapter I, Article IX of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and the Corresponding By-Laws.
SECTION 2. Eagles Club’s Name. Eagles Club duly organized in accordance with the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall adopt a name which shall precede the words Eagles Club.
SECTION 3. Charter Grant. Charter grant shall be bestowed upon a duly organized Region or Eagles Club, as the case maybe which shall have complied with the provisions of Article IX hereof and other related provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
A Region or Eagles Club shall only be considered duly affiliated to the Philippine Eagles after it shall have been given the Charter Grant.
The Charter Grant shall be the operative act which shall give official character to the affiliation and shall be given in accordance with PE Form I Article XVIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution, or duly reviewed and prescribed by the PEIL.
CHAPTER 10
ELIGIBILITY TO OFFICE
SECTION 1. Right to Office. The right to hold any office or position in the Philippine Eagles or in the Region or Eagles Club shall be bestowed upon to any qualified Eagle-members in accordance with this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 2. Eligibility to Elective National Positions. No Eagle-Member shall qualify to the position of a Regional Governor unless he shall have been a member in good standing of a duly organized and chartered Eagles Club of good standing at least two (2) years prior to the election and shall have satisfied and completed the mandatory seminar prescribed by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL) or particularly Leadership Seminar (LEADS).

--- Page 66 ---
SECTION 3. Eligibility to Appointive National Positions. No bonafide Eagle-member shall be appointed to any appointive National office or position unless he shall have completed the mandatory leadership seminar (LEADS) prescribed by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL) for elective and appointive national officials. The qualifications shall be possessed at the time of assumption to office but in no case shall an appointee be allowed to take his oath unless he shall have possessed all the qualifications to the office at the time of assumption thereof.
SECTION 4. Eligibility to Local or Eagles Club Positions. No bonafide Eagle-member shall be eligible to be elected or appointed to any Eagles club position unless he shall have completed the mandatory leadership seminar prescribed for Eagles club officers by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL); Provided, That a bonafide Eaglemember who shall have completed the seminar prescribed for national elective and appointive officers shall automatically be eligible to be elected or appointed to any National, Region or Eagles Club position.
SECTION 5. Mandatory Attendance to the Seminar on the Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024. All Eagle-members seeking elective and appointive positions are mandatorily require to attend the seminar on Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024.
CHAPTER 11
ELECTIONS SECTION 1. Conduct of Elections. All elections in the Philippine Eagles whether in the national, regional or Eagles club level shall be governed by the provisions of Article VII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and in conformity with the Rules duly promulgated by the Philippine Eagles Elections Commission (PhiEleCom).

--- Page 67 ---
CHAPTER 12
TERM OF OFFICE AND TENURE
OF ELECTED APPOINTED OFFICIALS
SECTION 1. Term of Office and Tenure of Elected Officials
a. Term of Office. The term of office of the National President, Executive National Vice President, National Vice Presidents, and Board of Trustees shall be for two (2) years without reelection on the same position, he is elected and occupied and shall officially commence on the first day of January following their elections on the last day of the annual National Congress of the Philippine Eagles which shall generally be held in the month of November unless there is force majeure, and shall end on the 31st day of December of the next succeeding Two
(2) Eagle Years.
b. The elections of the Regional Governor, Vice Governor, National Assemblymen in the Eagles Region; and the Eagles Club Officers of the Eagles Club shall be held in the months of September and October every year thereof and prior to the annual National Congress in November.
c. The term of office of Regional Governors, Other Regional Officers and Eagles Club officers shall be for one (1) year and commence on the first day of January following the elections and shall end on the 31st day of December of the same Eagle Year.
d. The term of office of Eagles Club Officers shall be for one year and shall officially commence on the first day of January following the elections and shall end on 31st day of December of the same Eagle Year.
e. Regional Officers or Eagles Club officers who may have served a midterm portion in office shall be deemed as having been held in a de facto capacity his term of office as if that it shall officially start on the first day of January following his

--- Page 68 ---
midterm election to the office and shall likewise end on the 31st day of December of the same said Eagle year.
f.

The term of office of the Executive Officers, National Commissioners, and other National Officers duly appointed by the National President shall also be one (1) year and shall be deemed to have commenced first day of January and shall end on the 31st day of December of the same said Eagle year subject to re-appointment at the pleasure of National President.

SECTION 2. Executive Officers and other Appointive National Officers.
The term of office of the executive officers and other appointive national officers shall officially commence on the date of their appointments and shall be co-terminous with term of office of the National President, unless he shall be given another appointment by the newly elected National President.
SECTION 3. Eagles Club Officers. The term of office of the Eagles Club President and other club officers shall be for one (1) year with re-election on the same position where he is elected and occupied which shall begin on January 1 and end on 31 December of the same Eagle Year.

--- Page 69 ---
CHAPTER 13
NATIONAL OFFICE AND JURISDICTION OVER ALL
EAGLES REGIONS AND CLUBS
SECTION 1. National Office. The National office of the Philippine Eagles shall be located in Quezon City, Philippines, or it may deem necessary.
SECTION 2. Jurisdiction Over All Eagles Regions and Clubs. The Philippine Eagles shall have and shall exercise jurisdiction over all Eagles Regions or Eagles Clubs duly chartered and affiliated within the Philippine Eagles as provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution, as well as, over Eagles Regions or Clubs and Affiliated Clubs which may have been chartered or formed in other countries as may be authorized by the National Assembly or Board of Trustees (Omnibus Amendment of 2008)
CHAPTER 14
PHILIPPINE EAGLES PROGRAM AND PROTOCOL
SECTION 1. Program and Protocol. The Philippine Eagles Program and Protocol shall be governed by the provisions of Article XIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and the Protocol Manuals to be updated and enacted by the National Assembly pursuant to the recommendations and endorsements of PEIL.
CHAPTER 15
NATIONAL CONGRESS
SECTION 1. National Congress. The Philippine Eagles National Congress shall be governed by the provisions of Article XVII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.

--- Page 70 ---
CHAPTER 16
ACCOUNTING AND AUDIT
SECTION 1. Accounting and Audit. The accounting and audit of the Philippine Eagles shall be governed by the provisions of Article XII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
CHAPTER 17
PHILIPPINE EAGLES FORUM
SECTION 1. Official Publication. The Philippine Eagles Forum shall be the official publication of the Philippine Eagles and shall be published every six (6) months, whether in print or electronically, if practicable and feasible.
SECTION 2. Forum Staff. The National President shall designate the editor/s and staff members of the Philippine Eagles Forum.
CHAPTER 18
PHILIPPINE EAGLES REGIONS
SECTION 1. Philippine Eagles Regions. The provisions of Chapters 1 and 2, Article IX hereof shall govern the Philippine Eagles Regions created pursuant to the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
CHAPTER 19
SEAL, COLOR EMBLEM
SECTION 1. Seal, Color, Emblem. The seal, color and emblem of the Philippine Eagles shall be as prescribed in Article XIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and as provided herein.

--- Page 71 ---
CHAPTER 20
PARLIAMENTARY AUTHORITY
SECTION 1. Rules of the National Assembly. The Rules of the National Assembly in Article VIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be the primary parliamentary authority governing its sessions and meetings as well as all meetings in Region, Eagles Clubs, Committees, Commissions, and Other Bodies of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 2. Applicability of National Assembly Rules to Regions, Clubs and other Eagles bodies. The Rules of the National Assembly shall be adopted as parliamentary authority in the meetings and deliberations of the regions, Eagles clubs, and other bodies of the Philippine Eagles.
CHAPTER 21
NATIONAL ASSEMBLY ACTS AND FORM
SECTION 1. Subsequent Acts. Subsequent Acts or Resolutions of the National Assembly shall be chronologically numbered per year and shall be in the form and manner provided in Article XVIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and as prescribed by the National Assembly.
