articles.summary: ARTICLE VII PHILIPPINE EAGLES ELECTION LAWS SECTION 1. Title. This Article shall be known and cited as the Philippine Eagles Election Laws. SECTION 2. Applicability. All elections in Philippine Eagles shall be conducted in the manner provided in this Article and by such other rul...
articles.content:
--- Page 72 ---
ARTICLE VII
PHILIPPINE EAGLES ELECTION LAWS
SECTION 1. Title. This Article shall be known and cited as the Philippine Eagles Election Laws.
SECTION 2. Applicability. All elections in Philippine Eagles shall be conducted in the manner provided in this Article and by such other rules and regulations that the Philippine Eagles Elections Commission (PhiEleCom) may promulgate and subject to the review and confirmation by the National Assembly, as far as practicable.
SECTION 3. PhiEleCom, Composition, Powers, Duties and Functions.
There is hereby created a Philippine Eagles Elections Commission herein after referred to as PhiEleCom consisting of a Chairman and four (4) Commissioners appointed by the National President based on geographical representation in Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao, as far as practicable. It is prescribed that PhiEleCom is not a law making body but a rule making body pertinent to elections in the Philippine Eagles.
The Philippine Eagles Elections Commission shall:
a. Have direct and immediate supervision and control over all matters pertaining to the conduct of elections of the Board of Trustees, all elective positions in National, Regional, and Eagles Club levels as prescribed herein and the enforcement of the provisions of this Article, as well as, over all officers of the Philippine Eagles who may be called upon said offices to perform duties relative to the conduct of elections, such as PEIL and others;
b. Promulgate such rules and regulations which shall implement all the provisions of this Article. The rules and regulations promulgated by the PhiEleCom shall be disseminated to all Eagles Regions and Eagles Clubs at least three (3) months prior

--- Page 73 ---
to the elections manually or electronically, as far as practicable;
c. Create and appoint such bodies or committees that shall assist the PhiEleCom in the effective and efficient conduct of elections;
d. Enforce and execute its decisions, resolutions, directives, orders or instructions on any matter affecting the conduct of elections: and
e. Perform such other powers, duties and functions whenever the interest of free, orderly and honest elections so requires.
SECTION 4. Organization of the PhiEleCom and Quorum. The PhiEleCom shall adopt its own rules and procedures. The presence of three
(3) members of the PhiEleCom shall constitute a quorum and the concurrence of the majority of the quorum shall be sufficient to pronounce or issue a resolution, ruling, directive and other similar acts.
The PhiEleCom shall appoint an Executive Director who shall handle its administrative business and affairs including the custody of records and documents. The PhiEleCom shall likewise appoint a PhiEleCom Treasurer.
SECTION 5. Disqualification of Members of the PhiEleCom. The Chairman or any Commissioner of the PhiEleCom shall not sit in any case in which he shall have known his bias, inclination, prejudice, hostility or antagonism against any candidate to the national position thereto and in connection therewith.
However, he may continue to participate in the hearing or withdraw from there, in accordance with his determination of the question of his disqualification.
In the event of disqualification of any member of the PhiEleCom, he shall be substituted by any member of the Philippine Eagles National Presidents’ League (PENAPLE) as recommended by the majority of the members of the PENAPLE in a meeting called for such purpose.

--- Page 74 ---
SECTION 6. National President May Appoint PENAPLE to the PhiEleCom.
The National President after due consultation may consider to appoint PENAPLE members to fill-up all positions in the PhiEleCom.
SECTION 7. National Elections. The national elections of all elected national officers shall be held annually on the last day of the annual National Congress held on the 3rd Saturday and Sunday of November or in a later date if there is a force majeure.
SECTION 8. Term of Office. The term of office of the Chairman of the PhiEleCom shall be two (2) years. For continuity and in order not to have disruption of election, the two (2) commissioners shall serve for a term of two years and the other two (2) for a term of one (1)
year. Thereafter, at the expiration of the term of office of those two
(2) commissioners appointed for one (1) year, all appointees in the PhiEleCom shall be for two (2) years. Their term of office shall be stated in the appointments issued by the National President.
SECTION 9. Confirmation of Appointments. The appointments of the Chairman and Commissioners of the PhiEleCom shall be submitted and confirmed by the Appointments Commission (APCOM).
SECTION 10. Postponement of Elections.
a. The PhiEleCom may postpone any national election under the circumstances herein defined, such as force majeure or analogous circumstances.
b. National elections of the national officers prescribed herein shall not be postponed except for serious cause such as force majeure, violence, terrorism, loss or destruction of election paraphernalia or records and other analogous causes, of such a nature that the holding of a free, orderly and honest election shall become impossible.

--- Page 75 ---
c. The PhiEleCom may declare that there is a failure of national election if, on account of force majeure, violence, terrorism or fraud, an election shall not have been held on date prescribed herein.
d. The resolution or ruling of the PhiEleCom declaring postponement of the national elections or a failure thereof may be appealed by any member of the National Assembly to the Supreme Tribunal within five (5) days from the promulgation thereof. The Supreme Tribunal shall resolve the appeal with dispatch five (5) days from receipt of the appeal and its decision shall be final and binding to all parties concerned.
SECTION 11. Certificate of Candidacy. Certificate of candidacy for Board of Trustees, National Elective Positions, Regional Governors, Vice Governors and National Assemblymen shall be duly accomplished in triplicate copies. The PhiEleCom shall retain two (2) copies and the third copy shall be sent to the Secretariat.
The certificate of candidacy shall be known as PhilEleCom Form 1 and shall be in the form as prescribed in Article XVIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 12. Election Propaganda. Candidates may avail of any form of election propaganda, manually or electronically provided it shall not have been prohibited by the PhilEleCom.
SECTION 13. List of Delegates.
a. The duly affiliated Regions shall certify to the PhiEleCom the list of its accredited delegates namely, Regional Governor, Vice Governor and three (3) National Assemblymen including the alternate National Assemblymen who shall be authorized to vote at the national elections at least twenty (20) days prior thereto. No Eagle-member shall qualify as a voting delegate unless he shall have been a member in good standing and

--- Page 76 ---
his Region likewise must be in good standing at the time of the elections.
b. Each Region in good standing shall be entitled to a maximum of five (5) regular voting delegates and to an equal number of alternate delegates, in case of the absence of the National Assemblymen.
SECTION 14. Board of Election Inspectors. The PhiEleCom shall constitute and appoint a Board of Election Inspectors consisting of a Chairman and two (2) members in good standing of a Region or Eagles Club, as the case may be; and Eagle-members in good standing at the time of their appointments.
SECTION 15. Official Ballots. The official ballots shall be known as PhilEleCom Form 7 and shall be in the form prescribed in Article XVIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 16. Voting time. The Board of Election Inspectors shall meet promptly at the polling place and at the time designated by the PhiEleCom during the elections and shall see to it that the voting shall be done and conducted in a peaceful, fair and orderly manner.
After the voting, the Board shall count publicly at the place designated by the PhiEleCom the votes cast and shall ascertain the results thereof.
After the votes shall have been counted, the Board shall immediately certify as to the results of the counting thereof and shall transmit the results to the Board of Canvassers.
SECTION 17. Board of Canvassers, Proclamation of Winners. The Board of Canvassers shall immediately proclaim the winners in the elections for the Board of Trustees, elective national positions, and in the case of Region, the Regional Governor, Vice Governor, three National Assemblymen and the alternate National Assemblymen after receipt of the certificate of canvass of the election from the Board of Election Inspectors or authorized regional PhiEleCom.

--- Page 77 ---
SECTION 18. Filing of Certificate of Candidacy. Any candidate running for the position in the Eagles Club, Region or even in the National position shall file a certificate of candidacy. No administrative fee or election fee shall be imposed by the PhiEleCom or any of its subordinates in all levels of election.
SECTION 19. Budgeting Support to PhiEleCom. The Philippine Eagles Elections Commission shall be allocated a sufficient and reasonable funds in the conduct of elections to cover the cost of the elections including per diem to the members of PhiEleCom.
SECTION 20. Suppletory Laws. Previous Philippine Eagles Election Laws which are inconsistent with the provisions of this Article and of this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be deemed repealed, otherwise, they shall have suppletory or supplementary application.

articles.title: Rules of the National Assembly
articles.summary: ARTICLE VIII RULES OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY RULE I. DEFINITION AND IDENTIFICATION As used in these Rules of the National Assembly, when capitalized:
articles.content:
--- Page 78 ---
ARTICLE VIII
RULES OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY
RULE I. DEFINITION AND IDENTIFICATION
As used in these Rules of the National Assembly, when capitalized:
a. “Rules” shall refer to the Rules of the National Assembly of the Philippine Eagles.
b. “Philippine Eagles” shall refer to The Fraternal Order of Eagles Philippine Eagles, Inc. (TFOE-PE, Inc.)
c. “National Assembly” shall refer to the National Assembly of the Philippine Eagles and shall be designated properly and consecutively, each year since 1980.
d. “Presiding Officer” shall refer to the incumbent National President of the Philippine Eagles or Designated Presiding Officer based on this Article.
e. “Regional Governor” shall refer to the duly elected governor of the Region and a Member of the National Assembly.
f. “Regional Vice-Governor” shall refer to the duly elected Vice-Governor of the Region and Member of the National Assembly.
g. “National Assemblymen” shall refer to the duly elected National Assemblymen of the Region and Members of the National Assembly.
h. “National Assembly Secretary” shall refer to the duly appointed Secretary of the National Assembly.

54

i.

“Members” shall refer to the both regular and ex-officio members of the National Assembly irrespective of whether they have voting rights or not.

j.

“Floor Leader” shall refer to the Floor Leader of the National Assembly and Chairman of the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee.

--- Page 79 ---
k. “Session” shall refer to the session or meeting regular or special of the National Assembly and may refer to the 1st, 2nd or 3rd Regular Session as may be necessary.
l.

“Committee” shall refer to the Standing Committees provided herein or created by the National Assembly it may deem as necessary, for the achievement of the goals and purposes of the Philippine Eagles.
RULE II. THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY COMPOSITION

1. The National Assembly shall be composed of:
a. Elected National Officials;
b. Regional Governors;
c. Vice-Governors;
d. National Assemblymen or their alternate National Assemblymen; and
e. Ex-Officio Members herein provided.
2. The Ex-officio Members shall be the Immediate Past National President and all past National Presidents of the Philippine Eagles, the Secretary General and all other ex officio Members of the National Assembly who shall have been given voting rights as provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
3. The Ex-officio members of the National Assembly who shall have the voting rights shall be the following:
a. The Immediate Past National President and the Incumbent Chairman of the Philippine Eagle National Presidents’
(PENAPLE) and all PENAPLE members;
b. The Secretary General; and
c. The Executive Director of the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (Omnibus Amendment of 2008)

--- Page 80 ---
4. All above mentioned Eagle-Members in Subsections 1, 2 and 3 are collectively called Members of the National Assembly, with equal right.
Before each session of the National Assembly, all Members shall take their Oath of Office.
5. The form of oath of the Members of the National Assembly shall be:

OATH OF OFFICE AS A MEMBER
OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY
“I Eagle (state name), having been duly elected/appointed as a Member of the National Assembly of The Fraternal Order of Eagles – Philippine Eagles, Inc. (TFOE-PE, Inc.), subscribing to its Eagles Constitution and believing in its capabilities as a self-reliant, First Philippine born fraternal socio-civic organization, do hereby solemnly make an oath that, I shall defend and uphold at all times, the said Eagles Constitution, as well as all laws, rules and regulations duly promulgated by the Philippine Eagles. And I shall consciously uphold at all times, the Eagles Delicadeza and Moral Code of Ethics, as the ultimate measure of my conduct and judgment relative to my dealings with the Philippine Eagles and fellow Eaglemembers of the National Assembly.
So Help Me God.”
_________________ Name of Eagle-Member

--- Page 81 ---
As far as practicable, all members of the National Assembly shall be present at the sessions of the National Assembly unless prevented beyond his control from doing so or if for justifiable reason his not being able to attend the same shall be expressed.
All Members of the National Assembly with voting right present at the session of the National Assembly shall vote on every question, bill or resolution under consideration.
RULE III. THE PRESIDING OFFICER
1. The incumbent National President shall be the Presiding Officer of the National Assembly.
2. The powers and duties of the Presiding Officer shall be, as follows:
a. To preside over the sessions of the National Assembly, as the case may be;
b. To preserve conduct and decorum during the sessions and in case of disturbance or disorderly conduct in the session hall, or committee meetings within its premises where the session or meeting is being held, take such measures as he may deem advisable or as the National Assembly may direct;
c. To decide on all questions of order or motions, subject to appeal by any Member of the National Assembly which appeal shall not be debatable, but any member appealing may explain his appeal for not more than three minutes; and
d. To sign all acts, measures, resolutions, memoranda and other papers or documents enacted or adopted by the National Assembly.
3. The Presiding Officer shall exercise other powers and duties vested in him by this Philippine Eagles Constitution and other acts or resolutions passed by the National Assembly.
4. The Presiding Officer shall yield the Chair to the Executive

--- Page 82 ---
National Vice President (ENVP) or in the latter’s absence to any of the National Vice Presidents, in case he shall have decided to participate in the deliberation of the National Assembly.
RULE IV. THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY SECRETARY
1. The National Assembly Secretary shall, at the commencement of each National Assembly, be elected by the National Assembly and shall hold office until his successor shall have been elected and qualified. Any vacancy occurring in the said office shall be filled in the same manner, until the vacancy shall have been filled, the Presiding officer may designate an Acting National Assembly Secretary. The elected National Assembly Secretary, preferably must have experience in any legislative work in any local or national bodies or must be a member of the Philippine Eagle for at least five (5) years.
2. It shall be the duty of the National Assembly Secretary:
a. To carry out or enforce orders and decisions of the National Assembly when such duty shall have devolved upon him;
b. To keep minutes of each session. The minutes shall comprise a clear and succinct account of business transacted and action taken by the National Assembly;
c. To call the roll of all the Members of the National Assembly before opening the session; read the minutes of the preceding session, by himself or through a reader designated by him with the authorization of the Presiding Officer; read the bills and proposed resolutions, messages, communications, memorials, petitions and other documents, which he should report to the National Assembly; or the reading whereof is required by the National Assembly or ordered by the Presiding Officer;
d. To note all questions of order with the decision thereon, the record of which shall be printed at the close of each session for the use of all Members;
e. To furnish and distribute to all Members, copies of acts,

--- Page 83 ---
measures, or resolutions or other documents, passed and adopted by the National Assembly within fifteen (15) days thereof, as far as practicable. Each member shall be entitled to a copy thereof, either manually or electronically; f.

To retain in his office two (2) copies of all acts, measures, resolutions or other documents passed and adopted by the National Assembly and to furnish the National Secretariat the same number of copies thereof within fifteen (15) days for its files and none shall be withdrawn therefrom without the written authorization from the National President and Secretary General;

g. To refer to the Floor Leader all bills, resolutions and matters received from any member as may be presented to the National Assembly;
h. To certify to the approval of all acts, measures and resolutions and other documents duly approved by the National Assembly and to attest and affix thereto the seal adopted by the National Assembly; and i.

To perform and discharge such other duties and functions as the Presiding Officer or the National Assembly shall direct him to do.
RULE V. SERGEANT-AT-ARMS

1. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall be elected by viva voce vote or acclamation of the majority of the present in attendance at the National Assembly at the commencement of each National Assembly annually and shall hold office until his successor shall have been duly elected or qualified. In case of vacancy of the office, the Presiding Officer may designate a temporary Sergeantat Arms who shall act as such until a regular Sergeant-at-Arms shall have been elected and qualified. Any elected Sergeant-atArms, preferably must have an experience in maintaining peace and order and must have been a member of the Philippine Eagles for at least five (5) years.

--- Page 84 ---
2. It shall be the duty of the Sergeant-at-Arms:
a. To attend the sessions of the National Assembly;
b. To maintain order in the session and committee meetings of the National Assembly under the direction of the Presiding Officer; and
c. To execute the orders of the Presiding Officer or of the National Assembly.
3. The symbol of office of the Sergeant-at-Arms shall be the Eagles Mace which shall be borne by him when enforcing the order in the National Assembly.
4. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall prohibit any person other than the Members of the Assembly to enter or stay within the session premises set aside for their exclusive use during the session.
5. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall strictly enforce the rules governing privileges of entrance to the session premises committee meetings and shall be responsible for the behavior of those permitted to enter in coordination with protocol officers.
6. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall keep inventory of paraphernalia and property of the Philippine Eagles used in the session and meetings of the National Assembly.
RULE VI. THE STANDING COMMITTEES
1. The National Assembly shall elect the following standing of 2024 committees:
a. Rules and Constitutional Amendments - This Committee shall have jurisdiction over all matters relating to the Rules of the National Assembly; amendments to the Philippine Eagles Constitution; order, manner and calendar of business transactions, as well as parliamentary rules and the creation of committee. The Chairman of the Committee shall be the Floor Leader of the National Assembly. The Vice-Chairman shall be the Assistant Floor Leader.

--- Page 85 ---
b. Membership - This Committee will review the list of members of the Philippine Eagles and the compliance on the rights and obligations of members as well as review of membership in the regions and Eagles clubs and their renewal annually.
c. Good Governance and Investigation - This Committee shall investigate and look into all matters relating to, malfeasance, misfeasance and non-feasance in office of any Executive, the National Assembly or any Member of the Supreme Tribunal of the Philippine Eagles including those of the national commissioners and officers whose offices are created by this Philippine Eagles Constitution or by the National Assembly.
d. Judiciary, Revision of Codes and Acts - This Committee shall have jurisdiction over bills, measures or resolutions involving revision of Codes or Acts of the Philippine Eagles, By-Laws and other related reforms in the Philippine Eagles, including the implementation of Rules and Regulations of enacted Codes and National Assembly Acts.
e. Finance and Appropriations. This Committee shall have jurisdiction relating to funds and expenditures of the Philippine Eagles and all matters on expenditures.
The National Assembly may create other committee it may deem necessary in furtherance of the goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles.
2. The Chairman of each Standing Committees shall be elected during the National Congress on the 3rd week of November and assume office on January 1 of the succeeding year and shall convene their Committee not later than January 15 of said Eagle Year.
3. No Member of the National Assembly shall be appointed Chairman of more than one Committee.

--- Page 86 ---
4. Each Committee shall have preferably at least twelve (12)
members of the National Assembly representing geographical jurisdiction in Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao who shall be appointed by its Chairman and on voluntary basis. The National Office shall appropriate a reasonable fund for each Committee for their effective and efficient discharge of duties and functions.
5. The Committee shall have regular or special meetings as may be agreed or decided by the Chairman or majority of the members.
6. In case of vacancy in the position of the Chairman of a Committee, the Vice-Chairman may discharge the duty of the Chairman or the same shall be filled immediately by the Presiding Officer.
7. When a Committee prepares its own bill which is called a National Assembly Committee Bill, it shall be referred to the Presiding Officer through the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee.
8. The Proposed Bills, Resolutions or Committee Report to be used in the National Assembly shall be pursuant to the forms to be prescribed by the Floor Leader and the National Assembly Secretary and included in the Manual of Procedures in the National Assembly.
9. Consideration of any report of the Committee on Rules and Constitutional Amendments shall take precedence of any report or matter and while pending the Presiding Officer shall not entertain any motion unless it be one for adjournment or recess or postponement of the consideration to another date.
The Presiding Officer shall not entertain any dilatory motion on the report.
RULE VII. THE FLOOR LEADER
1. The Floor Leader shall be the Chairman of the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee. He shall represent the

--- Page 87 ---
National Assembly in all matters which shall have to do with proposed measures and resolutions of any Member of the National Assembly or with Committee Report of any Committee submitted to the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee.
2. It shall be the duty of the Floor Leader:
a. To present to the floor of the National Assembly any proposed measure, resolution or Committee Report submitted to the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee;
b. To keep in touch with the Presiding Officer with respect to any proposed measure, resolution or Committee Report;
c. To confer with any Member of the National Assembly and Committee Chairman on their proposed legislative measures, proposals or resolutions;
d. To take to the Presiding Officer the sentiment of the National Assembly and to take to the National Assembly the sentiment of the Presiding Officer relative to the pending legislative measures proposal or resolutions; and
e. To perform, and discharge all other duties and functions as are observed in other parliamentary or legislative assemblies.
RULE VIII. THE SEAT
1. The Presiding Officer shall be seated at the head table while presiding during the sessions of the National Assembly.
2. The National Assembly Secretary shall be appropriately seated as near the head table where the Presiding Officer shall be seated.
3. Other officials of the National Assembly and the members shall be seated appropriately as arranged by the National Assembly Secretary in close coordination with the Sergeant-at-Arms.

--- Page 88 ---
RULE IX. THE SESSIONS
1. The regular sessions of the National Assembly shall be held every 3rd week of March, June and September of each year.
2. Special sessions may be called by the National President or by a petition in writing of the twenty percent (20%) of the members of the National Assembly, in good standing.
3. The Presiding Officer shall open the session by calling the National Assembly to order, after which there shall be observance of the following protocols a) recitation of the Philippine Eagles Universal Prayer b) singing of the National Anthem c) singing of the Philippine Eagles Hymn and d) recitation of the Eagles Pledge. Thereafter, the Presiding Officer shall order the roll call of the Members of the National Assembly by the National Assembly Secretary to determine the quorum.
4. The quorum of the National Assembly is by simple majority, provided notice shall have been given to all members of the National Assembly at least one (1) month before the scheduled National Assembly.
5. In case there is a question on quorum, the provision in Rule XX on Roll Call shall govern.
6. Upon the determination of the existence of a quorum, all members of the National Assembly shall take their Oath of Office as Members of the National Assembly as herein prescribed.
7. The session shall be held for members of the Philippine Eagles only and of the qualified members of the National Assembly as herein provided.
8. Sessions may be suspended or adjourned by the action of the National Assembly. The Presiding Officer may declare a recess when it deemed necessary or as required.
9. The exact hour of the opening and adjournment of the sessions shall be entered in the minutes thereof.

--- Page 89 ---
10. Except as provided in Rule XXI hereof, the Presiding Officer shall not allow any motion from any member on any ground for the suspension of these Rules.
11. The Presiding Officer shall close the session with the following:
“The session is adjourned.”
RULE X. THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY HALL
1. The place of session of the National Assembly shall be stated in the notice of National Assembly and corresponding session send to National Assembly members either manually or electronically.
2. The National Assembly Secretary shall see to it that notes of the debates and proceedings of the sessions shall have been taken and oversee the preparation of the minutes of the National Assembly.
RULE XI. ORDER OF BUSINESS
1. The Order of Business of the National Assembly shall be:
a. Call to Order
b. Entry of Mace
c. Entry of Colors
d. Recitation of Eagles Universal Prayer
e. Singing of National Anthem f.

Singing of Philippine Eagles Hymn

g. Recitation of Eagles Pledge
h. Roll Call i.

Reading and approval of the minutes of the previous session which may be dispensed upon action by the National Assembly

j.

Oath of Office as Members of the National Assembly

k. Reading and presentation of bills, measures, resolutions,

--- Page 90 ---
messages, communications, letters, petitions and the like, if any l.

Committee Reports, if any

m. Unfinished Business, if any
n. Business for the day, if any
o. Business for a certain date, if any
p. Unassigned business, if any
q. Bills, measures, resolutions, committee reports not completely tackled on first reading and presentation.
2. The minutes of the last proceedings of the National Assembly shall be submitted to the National Assembly for consideration and final approval thereof.
3. After the reading of the Order of Business, any Member or Committee Chairman who shall be recognized by the Presiding Officer and whose bill, measure, resolution or committee report is reported to the National Assembly for deliberation, adoption or approval shall speak and accordingly take the sponsorship thereof. Sponsorship shall be as briefly as possible.
4. The consideration of the Unfinished Business in which the National Assembly may be engaged at the time of adjournment shall be resumed until the unfinished business is disposed of.
5. After all pending business is disposed of the Presiding Officer shall call the business of the day.

--- Page 91 ---
RULE XII. THE CALENDAR OF BUSINESS
1. The Calendar of Business of the National Assembly shall be the following:
a. Unfinished business shall include business which was previously considered at the time of its last adjournment, of the immediate preceding session of the National Assembly.
b. Business for the Day shall include bills, measures, resolutions, committee reports and other legislative matters or acts set on the calendar for the consideration of the National Assembly for the day.
c. These may include proposal already deliberated upon or endorsed by the Regional Governors League (RGL), and the Vice-Presidents for Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao based on common and agreed proposals borne out by their respective geographical Congress or as discussed in RGL meeting.
d. Business for a certain date shall include any business which the National Assembly may set for consideration on a certain day. This may be proposed through a motion to be approved in open session.
e. Unassigned business shall include all bills, measures, resolutions, committee reports and other legislative matters or acts on which the Standing Committees concerned have already submitted reports and the consideration of which has not been definitely set or assigned by the Chairman of the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee or Floor Leader.

--- Page 92 ---
RULE XIII. BILLS, MEASURES, RESOLUTION,
COMMITTEE REPORTS AND OTHER LEGISLATIVE MATTERS
AND ACTS
1. Bills, measures, resolutions, committee reports and other legislative matters and acts shall be signed by their authors and shall be handed to the National Assembly Secretary who shall immediately transmit the same to the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee or the Floor Leader for report to the National Assembly. The full text of the bill, measure, resolution, committee report or legislative measure or act shall be read by the National Assembly Secretary or whomsoever he shall designate to read the same but said reading may be dispensed if copies thereof were distributed earlier to the Regional Governors or of the present members of National Assembly and the National Assembly by a majority vote shall approve that the reading be dispensed. Any proposal must state that it is based on excerpts from the minutes of a Regional Assembly and must be duly signed by the Regional Governor, Vice-Governor and National Assemblymen concerned.
2. Letters, messages, requests or petitions to the Philippine Eagles shall be read in full before the National Assembly. If need be, the same shall be referred to the proper Committee.
3. On consideration of a reported bill, measure, resolution, committee report or any legislative matter or act, the same shall be subject to debate, amendment and all proper parliamentary motions.
4. The National Assembly may, by a vote of majority, of those present close the debates at any time during the clarificatory questions and on all the amendments, if any. The motion toclose all debate shall be decided upon without debate.
5. After the general debate is closed and the amendments disposed of, the proposed bill, measure, resolution or other legislative

--- Page 93 ---
matter or act shall be voted upon for adoption or approval.
Those who shall have voted for adoption or approval shall enter their votes as YEAS (affirmative votes) and those who shall have disapproved as NAYS (negative votes). A majority vote of those present shall be sufficient for approval of a bill, resolution or Committee Report.
RULE XIV. MOTIONS AND THEIR PRECEDENCE
1. When a motion has been made, the Presiding Officer shall state the same to the National Assembly and it shall be then considered as having been brought to its attention. The motion may be withdrawn at any time before its decision or amendment.
An approved motion can no longer be withdrawn unless duly reconsidered.
2. When a question is under debate, no motion shall be entertained.
The exceptions, with their precedence in the following order, of motions, to wit:
a. To adjourn
b. To declare a recess
c. To lay on the table
d. To postpone to a certain day
e. To refer to appropriate committee f.

To amend; and/or

g. To postpone indefinitely.
Motions in the preceding paragraphs (a) to (d) shall be decided without debate
3. Motions to postpone to a certain day, to refer and/or to postpone indefinitely which shall have lost or did not adopt by the National Assembly, shall not be brought up again on the same day that they were presented.

--- Page 94 ---
4. While there are Members debating on the floor, a motion may be entertained only with their permission, as the case may be.
5. A motion to adjourn shall not be entertained when there is still a Member having the floor or while the sponsorship of any legislative measure or resolution is still going on. It shall not be entertained also when it is presented while voting is being called during the voting or on question of privilege.
6. Questions of Privilege of any member shall have precedence of all motions except a motion to adjourn.
7. There shall be an intervening business to justify a repetition of a motion to adjourn.
8. A Member who has yielded the floor for a motion of adjourn shall be entitled to prior recognition after the said motion is lost.
9. A motion for recess is without privilege and is not in order when a question of privilege is before the National Assembly. The Presiding Officer may entertain, in his discretion, a motion for a recess to prevent dilatory motions on the floor. The said motion, if entertained, shall be voted on upon by the members present.
No recess shall be allowed for a long period of time on any day of session as determined by the members present.
10. A motion to postpone does not have precedence of a motion to reconsider.
11. A motion to lay on the table is not debatable and shall be used for final disposition of a business, or to do away with the pending measure or resolution as report.
12. A motion to refer the matter to an appropriate committee shall have precedence over on motions to amend and to postpone indefinitely.
13. A motion to refer shall yield to motions to adjourn, to lay on the table, to postpone to a day certain and for the previous question.

--- Page 95 ---
14. A motion to postpone indefinitely opens to debate all the merits of the proposition.
15. A motion to postpone shall not be in order after the previous question has been ordered.
16. When a motion or proposition is under consideration, a motion to amend and a motion to further amend that amendment shall be in order and it shall also be in order to offer amendment by way of substitute bill, or resolution but the latter shalt not be voted on until the original motion or proposition is perfected and any of the amendments may be withdrawn before a decision shall have been taken.
17. No motion or proposition on a subject different from that under consideration shall be admitted under pretension of an amendment.
18. Amendments to the title of the bill, measure or resolution shall be decided without debate but it shall embody or reflect the body/provisions of such bill, measure or resolution.
19. When the reading of any document or paper, letter or communication before the National Assembly is demanded and the same is objected to by any Member, it shall be decided without debate by the vote of the majority of those present in the National Assembly.
20. A motion to read any part of these Rules is equivalent to a call to order and takes precedence of any motion other than to adjourn the motion.
RULE XV. QUESTIONS OF PRIVILEGE
1. Questions of privilege shall be:
a. Those questions affecting the rights of the National Assembly collectively including its safety, its dignity and the integrity of its proceedings.

--- Page 96 ---
b. Those questions affecting the rights, reputation and conduct of the National Officers, any member of the National Assembly, individually.
A Question of Collective Privilege may be raised by a statement or remark on the floor with respect to paragraph (a)
A Question of Personal Privilege may be raised by a statement of remark on the floor with respect to paragraph (b)
2. A Question of Collective Privilege maybe permitted on a matter concerning parliamentary procedure which affects the rights of a National Officer, any member of the National Assembly, individually.
3. A Question of Personal Privilege may be made on the floor even if the National Officer or any member of the National Assembly affected is not present.
4. A Member on a question of personal privilege shall disclose the involvement of his individual dignity in his representative capacity and shall confine himself to matters which affect his reputation or integrity as Member of the National Assembly.
5. A question of personal privilege shall not be used to attack a colleague in the National Assembly, mutual respect and observance of proper parliamentary language must be observed at all times.
6. Personal explanations (not a question of personal privilege) may be allowed only by unanimous consent of the members present at the National Assembly.
7. Questions of privilege shall take precedence of all other questions except motions to adjourn.

--- Page 97 ---
RULE XVI. PRIVILEGED QUESTIONS
1. Privileged questions are those motions or subjects matters under these Rules and other parliamentary practices and procedures take precedence of other motions and subject matters.
2. Privileged questions shall have precedence as determined in each case by these Rules or other parliamentary practices and procedures.
RULE XVII. THE SUSPENSION OF THE RULES
1. Except as provided in Rule XXI hereof, no motion shall be entertained to suspend these Rules during the National Assembly and National Congress.
RULE XVIII. DECORUM AND DEBATES
1. All Members of the National Assembly shall wear his Philippine Eagles uniform (Type A) and pin during the session of the National Assembly.
2. Any Member who shall have anything to say, talk or speak about, or shall intend to deliver a speech, to explain or discuss any subject before the National Assembly, shall rise and with courtesy address the Presiding Officer as “Mr. President.”, for recognition and to have the floor.
3. In case two or more Members rise together, the Presiding Officer shall name the Member who shall speak first and allow to have the floor.
4. The Presiding Officer motu proprio shall demand order and state that when there shall be two or more Members intending to speak, he shall have the authority to choose who shall speak first and have the floor.
5. Once a Member shall be recognized, he shall be entitled to have the floor and while he shall have the floor, no motion on a question of privilege shall be entertained.

--- Page 98 ---
6. The question of recognition shall not be subject to a point of order. There shall be no appeal from the decision of the Presiding Officer on a question of recognition.
7. No Member shall speak more than once on any question without leave of the National Assembly.
8. A Member who shall have been recognized by the Presiding Officer shall confine himself to the question under debate, avoiding personality and shall refrain from using words, phrases or any forms of expression or profane language, the meaning of which shall be unbecoming or inharmonious with the category inherent to and the standards of behavior accepted in, and of the position of Member of the National Assembly.
9. The Presiding Officer may admonish a Member on the floor to dwell only on relevant, pertinent and material issues and not on outside matters.
10. The Member of the National Assembly reporting or sponsoring a bill, measure, resolution, or committee report shall open and close the debate, as necessary. The presiding officer shall determine the period to open and close a debate.
11. A Member to whom sponsorship shall be yielded by another member or Member may yield or not to interpellations or for clarificatory questions.
12. A Member yielding to interpellation shall have the discretion whether to continue yielding or not regardless of the nature of interpellation or for clarificatory questions.
13. The interpellating Member shall confine himself to asking clarificatory question on subject matter and related issues.
14. With the permission of the Member, an interpellating Member may in turn be interpellate to clarify only pertinent questions raised.
15. A Member may reserve his right to speak against a bill, measure, resolution or any legislative matter or act.

--- Page 99 ---
16. A motion in the National Assembly to limit general debate on a bill, measure, or resolution, legislative matter or act, shall apply to the whole and not a part of the bill, measure or resolution.
17. Any Member not satisfied with the ruling of the Presiding Officer may appeal the decision from the ruling and call for a vote of those present in the National Assembly.
18. If a Member shall transgress or offend these Rules, the Presiding Officer or any other Member shall call him to order. If the call to order is appealed to, the National Assembly shall decide the case in accordance with paragraph 2, sub-paragraph (c), of Rule II of these Rules. If the decision is in favor of the Member, he shall proceed and shall have the floor. If the decision is against him, he shall yield the floor and sit down immediately.
19. A Member may ask the Presiding Officer that a Member in debate be called to order for words uttered on the floor which he deemed believe to be unparliamentary or profane language.
In such a case, he shall specify or repeat the words to which he is objecting.
20. A Member may move remarks be stricken off the record and may explain the reason for his motion.
21. The National Assembly shall have the power to impose sanctions on any Member for any unparliamentarily acts or behavior or for gross violation of these Rules and other instances specified under these Rules.
22. Observance of proprieties, such as decorousness and orderliness shall be required of the Members in the sessions of the National Assembly.
23. No Member shall be allowed when another is speaking to and pass between the latter and the Presiding Officer.
24. During sessions, the Members shall be in their respective seats and they shall not walk around or stand, unless recognized or

--- Page 100 ---
while the National Assembly is in recess.
25. A Member having the floor shall face the Presiding Officer and address the National Assembly properly.
26. Any Members who has the floor shall address each other in the third person.
27. No Member shall walk out across the session hall or premises while the Presiding Officer is addressing the National Assembly or a matter is being deliberated upon.
28. The Presiding Officer may speak from his Chair on questions of order and be first heard.
RULE XIX. VOTING
1. In putting a question, the Presiding Officer shall rise and do it in the following way: “As many as in favor (state the matter of question), say “YEAS”, and after the affirmative vote is expressed, he shall proceed as follows: “As many are as opposed, say “NAYS”.
The National Assembly may divide the house, and call for raising of the hands, if the Presiding Officer shall be in doubt on the results of YEAS and NAYS or if such division shall be demanded by a majority vote of those members present.
2. A vote by YEAS and NAYS shall be entered in the minutes of the session.
3. Any Member may explain his vote but not to exceed three minutes.
4. No motions except on the presence or lack of a quorum shall be entertained during the voting.
5. Where the voting resulted in a tie, the Presiding Officer shall cast his vote to break the tie.

--- Page 101 ---
RULE XX. ROLL CALL
1. The National Assembly Secretary shall prepare a list containing the names of Members of the National Assembly arranged per geographical representation and shall call the name per region as “Eagle Member RTD” or of the Members as “Eagle NP ABC”, when it shall come to a roll call for a vote or a call of the National Assembly.
2. A roll call may not be interrupted for a parliamentary inquiry or a question of personal privilege.
3. When a question of quorum shall be raised, the Presiding Officer shall ask the National Assembly Secretary to count the Members with voting rights present, and shall declare the presence of a quorum if such shall be the fact.
4. If the absence of a quorum shall be disclosed and raised, the only proceedings in order shall be the motions to adjourn and for a roll call of the National Assembly.
5. It shall not be the duty of the Presiding Officer to take cognizance of the absence of a quorum unless questioned by a point of order.
6. A quorum shall be presumed to the present unless a point of order is raised challenging its presence.
RULE XXI. RECONSIDERATION
1. When a bill, measure, resolution or any Committee Report shall have been adopted or lost, any Member voting with the majority that causes the adoption or loss may move for reconsideration of either action on the same day or following session day. This motion shall take precedence of all matters, propositions or questions, except a motion to adjourn.
2. A motion for reconsideration is a motion to cancel, vacate, annul or make void the action previously taken by the National Assembly.

--- Page 102 ---
3. A motion for reconsideration can only be proposed by any member who voted in the affirmative with the majority.
4. In the absence of a quorum, it shall not be in order to move to reconsider a vote on which a quorum shall be required.
5. The adoption of the motion for reconsideration shall open and cause a new or another discussion, debate and vote on a previously adopted or lost bill, measure, resolution, motion or Committee Report.
6. A motion to reconsider properly made is a privilege motion.
RULE XXII. NATIONAL ASSEMBLY DIALOGUE
1. The National Assembly shall set aside at least one session or meeting in a year for informal National Assembly dialogue, or as may be deemed necessary of all the Members. During this dialogue, matters and questions affecting the Philippine Eagles as a whole, in general, and the Regions or Eagles Clubs duly affiliated, in particular, shall be discussed exclusively.
2. The informal dialogue shall be devoted to the overall reexamination and re-assessment of the Philippine Eagles in all its phases of activities policies, programs and endeavors.
3. These Rules may be suspended while the National Assembly is holding an informal dialogue on the matters herein specified.
RULE XXIII. MEMBERS IN GOOD STANDING
1. No Member shall remain in good standing in the National Assembly unless he shall be a member in good standing of an Eagles Club duly affiliated with the Philippine Eagles which shall likewise be an Eagles Club and region in good standing.
2. A Member whose Eagles Club shall have lost its good standing in the Philippine Eagles may immediately affiliate himself to another Eagles Club duly affiliated to the Philippine Eagles after

--- Page 103 ---
following the procedures provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
3. The National Assembly shall by a vote of majority of those present declare any Member not in good standing for failure of his Region or Eagles Club to comply with its obligations to the Philippine Eagles. A certification to that effect from the National Secretariat duly signed by the Secretary General of the Philippine Eagles that a Region or Eagles Club is not in good standing shall be binding to the National Assembly.
Said Member shall re-acquire his good standing once his Region or Eagles Club shall have reacquired its good standing in the Philippine Eagles as may be certified by the Secretary General.
4. A Member who is not in good standing shall not be allowed to participate in any proceedings of the National Assembly until such time as he shall have re-acquired his good standing as provided in the preceding paragraph 3 hereof.
RULE XXIV. SANCTION AND DISCIPLINE
1. A Member who shall otherwise not be in good standing as specified in these Rules may be meted out such disciplinary action or sanction but in no case shall he be expelled or removed from the National Assembly.
2. Any of the following shall be ground for a disciplinary action or sanction of a Member of the National Assembly:
a. Gross or offensive violation or transgression of any of the provisions of these Rules;
b. Habitual failure to attend the sessions of the National Assembly without sufficient cause or reason. Said failure shall be presumed habitual if the Member shall have culpably or without justifiable reason absented himself from the sessions of the National Assembly for three (3) successive times; or

--- Page 104 ---
c. Gross failure to pay his dues and assessments, if any, as a Member of the National Assembly.
RULE XXV. ASSESSMENTS
1. The National Assembly shall determine the amount of assessment for each Member for the attendance and participation in the National Assembly.
2. The assessment shall be paid within the reasonable period prior to or at the time of the session.
3. The National Assembly shall designate among the Members, a National Assembly Treasurer who shall have custody of the funds of the National Assembly derived from the assessments and other sources. The National Assembly Treasurer shall be directed to open a bank account in any bank and deposit the National Assembly funds and money derived from the assessments and other sources subject to withdrawal with by the signatures of the National President and the National Assembly Treasurer or whosoever may be authorized by the National Assembly.
RULE XXVI. SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS
1. Insofar as they are not incompatible or inconsistent with these Rules, the following shall have supplementary force and effect:
a. Parliamentary Practices of the Congress of the Republic of the Philippines;
b. Rules of the House of Representatives. Commented and Annotated, Copyright 1963, by Inocencio B. Pareja; and
c. Annotated Rules of the Senate Procedures, precedents and practices of the Senate of the Philippines since 1946 by Honorata M. Orquiola, published in 1991.
In case of interpretation or construction of any of the provisions of these Rules, the majority of the members present at the National Assembly shall provide for the clear meaning and intent of these Rules based on parliamentary practices and procedures.

--- Page 105 ---
RULE XXVII. AMENDMENTS
These Rules may be amended or modified by two-thirds (2/3) votes of all the Members of the National Assembly present in its session duly called for the purpose.
RULE XXVIII. APPLICABILITY
These Rules shall apply to the deliberations in the National Assembly and meetings of the Standing Committees of the National Assembly and that of National Congress.
These Rules as far as practicable particularly on parliamentary rules and procedures may be applied in the meetings of the Eagles Club General Membership, Regional Assembly, or in any appropriate Philippine Eagles Commissions, or bodies in the Philippine Eagles.

articles.summary: ARTICLE IX PHILIPPINE EAGLES REGIONS, CLUBS AND DUES5 CHAPTER 1 THE PHILIPPINE EAGLES REGIONS
articles.content:
--- Page 106 ---
ARTICLE IX
PHILIPPINE EAGLES REGIONS, CLUBS AND DUES5
CHAPTER 1
THE PHILIPPINE EAGLES REGIONS
SECTION 1. The Philippine Eagles Region shall be created, chartered in the Philippines and in other countries or overseas and shall be given names and identification based on geographical location that comprise the provinces, cities and municipalities thereof, in the Philippine and demographic profiles in other countries or overseas.
SECTION 2. The Region Charter Grant. Each region must be composed of at least six (6) chartered male Eagles Clubs excluding Lady Eagles Club and each chartered Eagles Club must be composed of twenty five (25) Eagle-members before it will be given a charter grant as an affiliated region.
SECTION 3. New or Additional Eagles Regions. New or Additional Eagles Region may be added to the existing regions and may be created and chartered by the National President pursuant to the petition filed before the National Assembly. The creation and chartering of region through an appropriate National Assembly Resolution filed by the sponsor of the affiliated region shall be approved by the National Assembly. In case the National Assembly is not in session, and in extreme cases, the petition to create a region must be filed directly to the National President, copy furnish the National Assembly and the same shall be subject for confirmation.
SECTION 4. National Registry of Chartered Region. The list of chartered regions pursuant to this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be deposited in the national registry of the Philippine Eagles and with the National Secretariat. Copies of the National Registry shall be maintained in the National Office and by the National Assembly.
THIS ARTICLE WAS ENACTED ON MAY 27, 1989 AT UP AIT, DILIMAN, QUEZON CITY AND CITED AS THE
EAGLES CLUB AND REGION ACT OF 1989.
5

--- Page 107 ---
SECTION 5. Administrative Authorities, Powers, and Administration of the Eagles Regions. Each Eagles Region shall have administrative direction and supervision of its affairs and of all Eagles Clubs affiliated within the Region’s jurisdiction.
CHAPTER 2
THE REGIONAL GOVERNORS SUPERVISION OVER
THE EAGLES CLUBS UNDER THEIR REGIONS’ JURISDICTION
SECTION 1. Control and Supervision of Regional Governors on Eagles Clubs. All Regional Governors shall have control and supervision over the Chartered Eagles Clubs under their jurisdiction and may oversee the performance and compliance of the Eagles Clubs in accordance with the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 2. Regional Governor’s Power to Impose Penalty. A Regional Governor in good standing is hereby granted the power to impose penalty and sanctions to any erring Club Officers and/or members under his jurisdiction, including the recommendation of seizure of the Charter Grant, or de-activation of the Eagles Club, as the case maybe, after due notice and observance of due process.
SECTION 3. Sanctions to Erring Club Officers and Members under the Region’s Jurisdiction. Any erring Eagle-member may be suspended or expelled or meted out appropriate sanctions by the Regional Governor for any acts which it may deem inimical, harmful or prejudicial to the interest of the Eagles Club where such erring Eagle-member belongs, or any offenses committed to the Eagles Club, Region or the Philippine Eagles on the grounds such as inimical, harmful, or prejudicial to the interest of the Eagles Club, Region or National Fraternity.
The grounds for suspension or expulsion or other sanctions shall be solely determined by the Region concerned. The sanctions may only be imposed after due notice and observance of due process by the Regional Grievance Tribunal Committee which shall be created for

--- Page 108 ---
said purpose and the Committee’s decision shall by submitted to the Regional Governor for appropriate action. The Regional Grievance Tribunal Committee shall decide the matter referred to said Committee within thirty (30) days after receipt of the order from the Regional Governor to conduct said investigation.
The decision of the Regional Governor shall be appealable only to the Supreme Tribunal (ST). The ST shall decide the case within thirty (30)
days from receipt of the appeal by the aggrieved party or referral by the Region’s concerned. The appellant eagle-member shall submit and attach the decision being appealed incorporating thereto the decision of the Regional Grievance Tribunal Committee and other supporting documents or evidences. Failure of the ST to act on the appeal case after the lapse of thirty (30) days, the appealed decision of the Regional Grievance Tribunal Committee and/or Regional Governor shall become final and executory.
SECTION 4. Inherent Powers of the Regional Governor. In order to maintain harmonious relation in all Region, in addition to the powers vested and provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution, Regional Governor shall oversee the Eagles Clubs within his jurisdiction and may exercise inherent and incidental powers to this purpose.
SECTION 5. Grounds for Sanctions to Erring Members.
a. Any erring member may be suspended or expelled or meted out appropriate sanctions by the Eagles Club for any acts which it may deem inimical, harmful or prejudicial to the interest of the Eagles Club or to the Philippine Eagles.
b. The grounds for suspension or expulsion or other sanctions shall be determined by Eagles Club and by the region or Supreme Tribunal on appeal. The sanctions may only be imposed after due process by the Region or Eagles Club Grievance Tribunal Committee which may be created for said purpose and their decision shall be final and executory subject to appeal procedure hereof or as may be enacted by the National Assembly.

--- Page 109 ---
c. No Eagles Club shall admit as its member any suspended or expelled member of another Club.
d. The cliché that “Once an Eagle, always an Eagle” shall no longer hold true with the above cited provisions.
CHAPTER 3
EAGLES CLUBS
SECTION 1. Membership to the Philippine Eagles. Membership to the Philippine Eagles shall be by Eagles Club. The Philippine Eagles shall be composed of the Eagles Regions and affiliated Eagles Clubs duly organized, chartered and affiliated to the Philippine Eagles and in accordance with this Philippine Eagles Constitution and related rules and regulations. Applicant shall become an Eagle-member after undergoing the 5Is, namely Introduction, Interview, Indoctrination, Incubation, and Induction as prescribed in Policy Manual.
SECTION 2. Eagle-Members. Each Eagles club shall have at least twentyfive (25) bonafide male Eagle-members at the time of its creation and chartering. Membership to the Eagles club shall be by sponsorship by any bonafide and affiliated Eagles Club: Provided, That the required membership number may increase subject to review and approval of the National Assembly. Membership to any Eagles Club shall be open to any male or female person who shall be of age at least 26 years old, of good moral character and reputation in the community and shall be actively and gainfully engaged in some business, profession or gainful occupation. Any member in good standing of duly chartered Eagles Club in good standing shall be given a permanent number which shall be recorded and filed by the National Secretariat in the National Registry or Book of Membership of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 3. Lady Eagles or Female Eagle-Members. Wives or ladies of bonafide Eagle-members may organize a Lady Eagles Group under the auspices of the Chartered Male Eagles Club to which the bonafide Eagle-members belong but the formation of such group shall be

--- Page 110 ---
complementary and auxiliary to and subject to the direction and control of the Eagles Club who organized or sponsored the same.
The Lady Eagles if desired and agreed may be organized as one national group under the Chairperson of the Lady Eagle of the National President.
SECTION 4. Eagles Club’s Name. Eagles Club organized and chartered in accordance with the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall adopt a name which shall precede the words Eagles Club.
SECTION 5. Classes of Membership. Membership to the Philippine Eagles shall either be active or inactive.
Active member. An active member shall be a bonafide Eagle-member.
A bonafide Eagle shall be one who is a member in good standing of a duly chartered Eagles Club in good standing.
Inactive member. An inactive member shall refer to an Eagle-member who shall have meanwhile ceased to be a bonafide Eagle and who fails to perform his obligations as prescribed herein.
Eagles-on-site. The Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS) duly selected by the Eagles Club, may be given the rights and privileges of an Eaglemember. To be conferred as Eagle-on-site, GOHAS must possesses the qualities of Eagleism and who adhere to the principles of the Philippine Eagles. The acceptance by the GOHAS to be an Eagle-onsite will be at his or her option.
SECTION 6. Rights, Privileges, Duties and Obligations of Active Members.
An active Eagle-member shall have rights, privileges, duties and obligations, as follows:
a. He shall have all the rights and privileges inherent in his membership to a duly chartered Eagles club and, if qualified, shall have the right to vote and be voted for any position in

--- Page 111 ---
his Eagles Club or in the Philippine Eagles as provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution;
b. He shall be given and assigned a permanent number in the Philippine Eagles and must be listed in the National Registry or Book of Membership, as the case may be;
c. He shall have duties and obligations inherent in his membership and the obligations shall include payment of national, regional or club dues and other financial obligations implicit in his membership; and
d. He shall promote the good name, image and reputation of the Philippine Eagles, his Region and his Club and shall assert a course of conduct reflective of the ideals of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 7. Rights, Privileges, Duties and Obligations of Eagle-on-site.
The Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS) who accepted the invitation of the duly affiliated Eagles Club to be an Eagle-onsite shall have rights, privileges, duties and obligations as follows:
a. All the rights, privileges, duties and obligations as prescribed in the preceding Section;
b. The right to be called Kuya or Ate;
c. After one (1) year of being as an Eagle-on-site, the right to be a regular member upon payment of national, regional, and club dues and other financial obligations; and
d. The right to be appointed or elected as officer of the panel of national, regional or club eagles-on-site.
SECTION 8. Region and Eagles Club Charter Grant. The National President shall sign and present the Charter Grant to a newly organized Eagles club or region and duly affiliated to the Philippine Eagles after completion of the Mandatory Orientation Seminar. The Secretary General shall attest to giving of the Charter Grant which shall be

--- Page 112 ---
confirmed to by the Club Charter President, the Executive Director of PEIL and the Vice-President of Luzon, Visayas or Mindanao concerning their geographical jurisdiction, shall likewise attest to the giving of the Charter Grant. The Regional Governor shall also attest to the giving of the charter grant, to the Eagles club under his jurisdiction.
(Omnibus Amendment of 2008).
SECTION 9. Text of the Charter Grant. The text of the Charter Grant shall conform to PE Form 1 as prescribed in Forms, Article XVIII, of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 10. Pre-requisites to Charter Grant. No Eagles club shall be granted its Charter Grant by the Philippine Eagles without prior settlement of the required national, regional and club dues and other financial obligations and prior compliance with the pre-requisite and Mandatory Orientation Seminar prescribed by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL) as created and prescribed by this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 11. Chartering Policies. Old Eagle-members of an affiliated Eagles Club, in good standing who shall join the creation and chartering of a new Eagles Club by becoming one of its Charter officers or members shall equally pay in full all the dues and fees imposed by the Philippine Eagles. The inclusion of old and new Eagle-members for historical and posterity privileges in the Charter Grant are recognized and such chartering may confer upon equal rights and privileges upon Charter members. Henceforth, only Eagle-members in good standing shall be allowed to form a new Eagles club and have their names inscribed in Charter Grant. The process of determining of good standing shall focus on the Eagle-members current payment of national, regional and club dues on the current Eagle Year, date or period of chartering as determined by the National Treasurer, the concerned Regional Governor and the Eagles Club President of

--- Page 113 ---
the old Eagle-members desiring to join such chartering. In addition, expelled or suspended members shall in no case take no part in such activity. (Eagles Membership Reform Act of 2019)

SECTION 13. Membership Transfer. An Eagle-member shall be free to transfer to any Eagles Club of his choice, such transfer shall not be construed as an interruption of his membership as a bonafide Eagle-member.
SECTION 14. Transfer or Reactivation. Transfer membership or membership reactivation shall be allowed subject to the usual obligation of an Eagle-member to pay and settle all financial obligations to the Eagles Club and Region concerned, upon proper notice and securing the permit to transfer, which shall be given without any other conditions, except settlement of all dues and financial obligations and with due notice on request to transfer and revocation at least thirty (30) days prior to such transfer.
SECTION 15. Requirements for Transfer. No membership transfer shall be allowed unless such Eagle-member applying for transfer pays in full all current dues and arrears as may be lawfully claimed or imposed by the original Eagles Club. Upon compliance, the transferee shall be issued a certificate of eligibility to transfer. No Eagles Club shall be allowed to admit a transferee unless he shall present the certificate of eligibility to transfer for the purpose. If regularly admitted, the transferee shall comply with all the requirements imposed by the receiving Eagles Club, including the payment of all dues imposed on regular members therein. Due notice to his previous Eagles Club and receiving Eagles Club shall be filed both by a transferee Eaglemember simultaneously.
SECTION 16. Membership Reactivation. An inactive Eagle-member may be allowed to regain an active status and thus renew his rights to enjoy membership benefits and privileges upon full payment of his standing accounts payable, including current dues and penalties where applicable as the Eagles Club and Region may require. After settling the financial obligations and the Eagle-member could resume active membership status, non-interruption of his bona fide membership shall be assumed in his favor.

--- Page 119 ---
SECTION 17. Membership Deactivation. Eagles Club membership to the Philippine Eagles may be deactivated for failure of Eagle-member to pay his national, regional and club fees and dues and other financial obligations to the Philippine Eagles. Membership to the Eagles Club may also be deactivated for failure to pay the Eagles club dues and other financial obligations as prescribed by the Eagles Club and any acts harmful and prejudicial to the interest of the Eagles Club, after due process.
SECTION 18. Eagles Club Constitution. The Eagles Club shall preferably have a Constitution and By-Laws as well as Eagles Primer of its own and shall be in accordance with PE Form 4 on Forms, Article XVIII, of this Philippine Eagles Constitution. Such Constitution and By-Laws shall conform and adhere to the provisions and tenets of this Philippine Eagles Constitution, and that of the Region, if any.
SECTION 19. Eagles Club Banner. The Eagles Club shall have a banner in such design as shall have been prescribed in Article XIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and shall follow strictly the dimension mentioned therein.
SECTION 20. Club Fiscal Year. The fiscal year of the Eagles Region or Eagles Club shall start on January 1 and shall end on December 31 of the same year.
CHAPTER 4
JUNIOR EAGLES CLUB
SECTION 1. Authority and Sanction to Organize Junior Eagles Club.
Junior Eagles Club shall be organized in accordance with this Chapter.
SECTION 2. Goals of Junior Eagles Club. The Junior Eagles Club as an auxiliary of the sponsoring Eagles Club shall:

--- Page 120 ---
a. Provide a forum for healthy fellowship, brotherhood ties, service, thoughtfulness and helpfulness among the members and to others;
b. Develop constructive and quality leadership and personal integrity among the members;
c. Awaken the awareness of the members on the importance of home and family;
d. Develop and inculcate in the minds of the members their sense of nationalism and of loyalty to country;
e. Inculcate in the minds of the members the importance of taking and accepting individual responsibility as a basis for personal success; and f.

Help in their community and engage in worthwhile projects and programs.

SECTION 3. Name of Junior Eagles Club. A Junior Eagles Club shall adopt a name which shall precede the words Junior Eagles Club.
SECTION 4. Membership.
a. Any unmarried, male or female person, whose age is between 15 to 25, and of good moral character and who shall be able to devote his or her time to the Junior Eagles Club, shall be eligible to be a member of Junior Eagles Club.
b. Any bonafide and affiliated Eagles Club and or Eagle-member may propose the formation and organization of a Junior Eagles Club submitting the application for membership of the proposed members thereof to the Regional Governor of the Eagles region concerned for the deliberation and approval of the Regional Assembly, as the case may be, thereafter submission to the National Office for grant and recognition.

--- Page 121 ---
SECTION 5. Sponsorship Fees. A Junior Eagles Club may be sponsored by an affiliated Eagles Club or by a bonafide Eagle-member whose Eagles Club shall be in good standing. The sponsoring Eagles Club or Eagle-member shall be responsible to defray the expenses incidental to the formation and chartering of the Junior Eagles Club.
SECTION 6. Club Recognition. The National President of the Philippine Eagles shall grant and extend recognition to a Junior Eagles Club which may be formed and organized in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter. The recognition of the Junior Eagles Club is through a Creation Grant.
SECTION 7. Seminar as Pre-condition to Recognition.
a. No recognition shall be granted and extended to any Junior Eagles Club without first undergoing the Mandatory Orientation Seminar which shall be prescribed by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL) or may be given by the Region’s Rosei Director, if any.
b. The Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership shall prepare and prescribe the curriculum of the Mandatory Orientation Seminar for Junior Eagles Club.
SECTION 8. Harmony and Adherence. The Junior Eagles Club shall adhere to the Philippine Eagles Constitution, as well as to all the laws which may hereafter be promulgated by the National Assembly.
The Junior Eagles Club shall not adopt or take any course of conduct or action contrary to, or in derogation of the goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 9. Withdrawal of Recognition. The recognition extended to any Junior Eagles Club may be withdrawn at any time for any act of the Junior Eagles Club which may be contrary to, or in derogation of the goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles.

--- Page 122 ---
SECTION10. Existing Junior Eagles Clubs. Junior Eagles Club formed prior to this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be given a period of six (6) months from approval hereof within which to comply with the requisite Mandatory Orientation Seminar (ORIENTS) prescribed in this Chapter.
SECTION 11. Constitution and By-Laws. The Junior Eagles Club shall have a Constitution and By-Laws in the manner prescribed in PE Form 20, Article XVIII, of this Philippine Eagle Constitution and shall conform and adhere to the provisions and tenets hereof.
CHAPTER 5
LADY EAGLES GROUP
SECTION 1. Lady Eagles Group. Wives or ladies of bonafide Eaglemembers may organize a Lady Eagles Group either in the Eagles Club level or in the national level. Subject to the approval of the Eagles Club, if it shall have been organized within the male Eagles Club, or of the Philippine Eagles, if it shall have been organized in the national level. The Lady Eagles Group shall undertake projects which shall be complementary and consistent with the goals and objectives of the Eagles Club and Eagles Region of the Philippine Eagles. The created Lady Eagles Club is an auxiliary of the sponsoring Eagles Club.
SECTION 2. Recognition of Lady Eagles Club. Lady Eagles Club shall have at least fifteen (15) members at the time of its creation and Lady Eagle-member must have the qualifications to help in the furtherance of the goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles.
The recognition of the Lady Eagles Club is through a Creation Grant

--- Page 123 ---
CHAPTER 6
AGGRUPATION OF EAGLES REGIONS
SECTION 1. Aggrupation of Eagles Regions. The chartered Eagles regions may form an aggrupation of Eagles regions based on geographical location namely, Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, and as the National Assembly may enacted.
SECTION 2. National Vice President, For Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.
The duly elected Regional Governors shall constitute themselves into a body of the Eagles Regions to which they shall have belonged. The Group of Eagles Region shall be headed by a National Vice President of the geographical location as mentioned in the preceding Section, duly elected by the delegates of the National Congress on the last day of the annual National Congress of the Philippine Eagles, which shall generally be held in the month of November unless there is force majeure.
The National Vice President of each geographical location shall be its Chief Executive and the Presiding Officer of the meetings or Congress of the aggrupated regional governors of said body.
The aggrupated regional governors shall be the policy-making body of the Eagles regions concerned and may pass and adopt regional measures and resolutions but must conform to this Philippine Eagles Constitution, By-Laws, Acts and Resolutions passed and adopted by the National Assembly.
SECTION 3. The National President Power to Appoint Acting Regional Governor. The National President has the power to appoint a qualified Eagle-member as an Officer in Charge (OIC) or Acting Regional Governor in any Eagles Region where no regional governor shall have been elected or if the same is vacated. Said appointee Regional Governor shall be an ex-officio member of the National Assembly but shall have no voting right.

--- Page 124 ---
CHAPTER 7
REGIONAL GOVERNORS LEAGUE
SECTION 1. The Regional Governors League.
A. In order to assist the national leadership in the pursuit of the goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles, the duly elected Regional Governors shall form a national association of all Regional Governors to be called the Regional Governors League (RGL).
B. The RGL is a strong bond of regional governors formed in the concept of Alalayang Agila.
SECTION 2. The RGL Chair and Officers. The RGL Chair and officers shall be elected by the Regional Governors during the last day of the National Congress held annually on the 3rd week of November unless there is force majeure, under the control and supervision of the PhiEleCom. The RGL Chair shall be assisted by its duly elected or appointive officers to perform its duties and functions under its adopted By-Laws.
SECTION 3. The RGL Roles. The RGL Roles and Duties in the Philippine Eagles are as follows:
a. Help in the formulation of policies in the Philippine Eagles through proposed bills or resolutions common or adopted by the majority members of the RGL and for consideration by the National Assembly;
b. Help in shepherding of the priority measures and agenda of the National President through a healthy discussion and deliberation among the regional governors and such agreed measure shall be submitted to the National Assembly and be given priority in the calendar;
c. Discuss and adopt common projects and programs in
