d. Conduct joint community outreach and humanitarian service among the Regional governors in order to secure and pool resources and provide greater and wider help to the needy; and
e. Perform such other roles and duties that the National President may delegate.
SECTION 4. Authority of the RGL to formulate its own Rules and ByLaws. The RGL may adopt and promulgate its own Rules and By-Laws governing its membership, meeting, election of officers, conduct and discipline its members after due process, if desired: Provided, That such Rules and By-Laws shall be consistent and must conform and adhere to the provisions of this Philippine Eagles Constitution and that of National Assembly Acts and Resolutions.
ARTICLE X
PHILIPPINE EAGLES INSTITUTE OF LEADERSHIP
SECTION 1. Title. This Article shall be known and cited as the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership Act (PEIL) or PEIL Rules of 20246.
SECTION 2. Creation and Composition of the Institute. There is hereby created the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership hereafter referred to as PEIL, a collegial body composed of PEIL Directors as provided in the next succeeding sections, hereof.
“SECTION 3. Interim Directors of the Institute: Term: Duties and Functions. – (In recognition of the PEIL Rules of 1989, the provisions on Interim Director of PEIL are hereby retained for historical purpose and reference.)
Created on May 27, 1989 at UP AIT, Diliman, Quezon City under Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership Act of 1989. Said Act was amended in 2008 and further amended by this 2024 Rules 6

--- Page 126 ---
a. The first directors of the Institute shall be called interim directors.
and shall be composed of incumbent directors of the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership created under GA Act No. 4 (1984)
and of the incumbent National President and all past national presidents of the Philippine Eagles who are not incumbent of the former. They-shall serve for a term of one (1) year from approval of this Magna Carta.
b. The interim directors shall formally organize themselves into a collegial interim Institute within one (1) month from the approval of this Magna Carta and shall elect among themselves its Executive Director.
The interim Institute may designate a seminar director who shall conduct a seminar from time to time under the direct supervision of the interim Institute.
c. The Interim Institute:
1. Shall prepare a uniform curriculum prescribing the manner, scope and extent of the orientation seminar and of the leadership seminar as prescribed in this Book and in this Magna Carta;
2. Shall hold and conduct a national leadership seminar within two (2) months from the approval of this Magna Carta to be participated in by the qualified Eagles from all Eagles Regions and Clubs and shall select and appoint from said participants, such qualified seminar discussants who may be authorized to conduct and give seminars in their respective regions; and
3. Shall undertake, perform and discharge, to the extent that it shall be able to do, the powers, duties and functions of the Institute as prescribed in Section 7 of this Article.
d. The acts, proceedings and deliberations of the interim Institute shall form part of this Book.”

--- Page 127 ---
SECTION 4. PEIL Directors and their Term of Office.
a. Composition of the Institute. The Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership which shall hereafter be briefly referred to as PEIL shall be composed of an Executive PEIL Director (EPD)
who shall be its head and as many qualified PEIL Directors as needed by the Philippine Eagles, all of whom shall be appointed by the National President after assessment and qualifications as herein prescribed in Section 5 hereof.
The PEIL Directors shall elect from among themselves the Executive PEIL Director (EPD).
b. Term of Office of the EPD. The term of office of the Executive PEIL Director (EPD) shall be for two (2) years. The PEIL Directors shall elect among themselves the EPD on the 3rd week of November during the National Congress: Provided, That, the elected EPD shall assume office on January 1 of the succeeding year and shall serve two (2) years thereafter.
c. Term of Office of PEIL Directors. The qualified and appointed PEIL Directors shall enjoy security of tenure subject to the provisions of paragraphs (c) and (f) of Section 6 hereof. The National President shall appoint the PEIL Director pursuant to the provisions of Section 5 hereof on Qualifications of PEIL Directors.
d. Appointment of At Least Three (3) Senior PEIL Directors. To ensure the educational and academic quality and directions of seminars held and given by PEIL, the incumbent National President shall see to it that at least three (3) Senior PEIL Directors (SPD) shall be occupying the positions of SPD in any Eagle Year, simultaneous with that of PEIL Directors.
Provided, That, those who served as Executive PEIL Director shall automatically be appointed as Senior PEIL Director, upon the expiration of his term of office as EPD or upon serving one Eagle Year: Provided, Further, That, those who have been appointed SPD in consideration of their long

--- Page 128 ---
service as PEIL Director shall be recognized and given weight by the National President in appointing SPD.
e. Secretary General as Ex-officio Member of PEIL. The incumbent Secretary General shall be an ex-officio PEIL Director whose term of office as a PEIL Director shall be coterminus with his term of office as the Secretary General. He shall have a voting right as an ex-officio PEIL Director in the meetings and voting of PEIL.
f. Rule-making power of PEIL. Laws previously enacted either by the abolished General Assembly and/or by the present National Assembly which has replaced the former and authorizing and giving PEIL the powers to prepare separate manuals, primers, or guidelines on any or all Articles of the Philippine Eagles Constitution; to prepare guidelines on Junior Eagles Club; to prepare various Eagles Forms; and to prepare uniform; guidelines on the Eagles program and protocol; entry of colors; entry of mace; Eagles Universal Prayer; reception and escorting of guests; master of ceremonies; turnover ceremonies; rituals and other matters relative to Article XIII of the Philippine Eagles Constitution are hereby made integral parts of this Article.
SECTION 5. Qualifications of PEIL Directors of Institute. The PEIL Directors shall have the following qualifications:
a. He shall be a bonafide Eagle-member and shall have served as an Eagles Club President or as Regional Governor, or shall have been elected or appointed to any national position of similar or higher category of that a regional governor;
b. He shall have mandatorily completed the leadership seminar prescribed by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL). He shall be adequately familiar with the Philippine Eagles in general, this Philippine Eagles Constitution, National Assembly Acts or resolutions, institutional goals, objectives,

--- Page 129 ---
principles, philosophy, and practices and precedents of the Philippine Eagles;
c. He shall be willing and prepared to commit his time to the PEIL without any honorarium or compensation but with reasonable per diem as prescribed;
d. He shall pass the assessment and evaluation conducted by the Screening Committee of PEIL, created upon the directive of the EPD. The Screening Committee shall be composed of EPD, SPD, PD, and a representative from PENAPLE; and
e. He shall submit himself to such further seminar or learnings after he shall have been appointed to the PEIL to intensify his knowledge of the Philippine Eagles, the Philippine Eagles Constitution, institutional goals, objectives, and principles, philosophy, National Assembly Acts or resolutions.
No director of the PEIL shall be appointed to any national position of the Philippine Eagles during his incumbency, unless if it is in the exigency of service, or his expertise is needed in the Philippine Eagles:
Provided, However, That, he shall be qualified to any position in his region or Eagles club.
SECTION 6. Duties and Functions of the Executive PEIL Director (EPD).
– The Executive PEIL Director shall perform the following duties and functions:
a. To supervise and oversee the performance of duties and obligations of PEIL Directors as herein prescribed;
b. To attend the National Assembly and National Congress as an ex-officio member with voting right;
c. To recommend to the National President the revocation of the appointments of any PEIL Director for any acts that are inimical, harmful, and prejudicial to the interest of the PEIL, after due process;
d. To authorize the conduct of MANDATES as provided hereof to the PEIL Directors;

--- Page 130 ---
e. To conduct preliminary assessments on the merits, ethics, and qualifications of any candidates for the position of PEIL Director, before his appointment shall be issued by the National President; f.

To recommend the revocation of the appointment of any regular PEIL Director to the National President, for failure to maintain merit and fitness as a PEIL Director, after careful review and due process; and

g. Perform such other functions and duties as may be delegated by the National President and/or by the National Assembly.
SECTION 7. Autonomy and Institutional Role of the PEIL. The PEIL shall be the educational, training, and leadership arm of the Philippine Eagles. To the extent as defined in this Article, it shall enjoy autonomy in the performance of its powers and in the discharge of its duties and functions.
SECTION 8. Powers, Duties and Functions of the PEIL. The PEIL shall:
a. Prepare and prescribe the curricula for orientation and leadership seminars geared towards intensifying the member’s knowledge, faith, belief, commitment and adherence to the Philippine Eagles;
b. Prepare and prescribe the scope, extent and manner of holding seminars as prerequisite for the issuance of a certificate of attendance or certificate of completion, as the case may be;
c. Issue, together with the National President and attested to by the Secretary General and by the National Vice President of the Region concerned, orientation certificate or leadership certificate, to those who shall have taken and completed the prescribed seminars and deliver immediately to the Secretary General for file and recording in the National Secretariat after the conclusion of the seminar the original copy of the list of participants to the seminar;

--- Page 131 ---
d. To strengthen PEIL by institutionalizing learnings, practices, rituals and protocols through continuing conduct of education and seminar in all levels of the Philippine Eagles;
e. Prepare primers and guidelines on any or all Articles of this Philippine Eagles Constitution; f.

Prepare uniform form of reports prescribed for Eagles Clubs and Regions;

g. Promulgate rules and regulations as may be necessary to carry the objectives of the PEIL;
h. Perform such other duties and functions peculiar and inherent to the PEIL geared towards improving and enhancing the prestige of the Philippine Eagles and of the PEIL; i.

Propose rituals for the Philippine Eagles for consideration and approval of the National Assembly and submit quarterly report of the seminars conducted to the National President;

j.

To develop online courses, in-person training and mentorship among Eagle-members;

k. To provide Eagle-members with knowledge and learning they need to grow and develop, and that Eagle-members know their roles in helping the Philippine Eagles for the furtherance in achieving its goals, objectives and purposes through on-line courses, during extreme time and pandemic, and in-person training and mentorship; l.

Hold, conduct and sponsor seminars or symposia on any current matter of national interest or importance which shall be informative, educational or beneficial to the Eaglemembers, in particular, or the country in general, in such case, the PEIL shall submit a report to the National Assembly of the conduct and result of the seminar within fifteen (15)
days before the session of the National Assembly; and

m. Propose the establishment and creation of the Philippine Eagles Academy (PEA) to institutionalize learnings and

--- Page 132 ---
education in the Philippine Eagles and support said PEA in its initial years.
SECTION 9. Mandatory Seminars or MANDATES. The mandatory seminars or MANDATES in the Philippine Eagles shall be the Orientation Seminar briefly called ORIENTS; the Leadership Seminar briefly called LEADS; the National Officers’ Seminar briefly called NOSE; Spiritual Awareness and Values Education Seminars (SAVES); and other to be mandated by the National Assembly.
a. ORIENTS; objectives; to whom and by whom given. ORIENTS is designed to familiarize applicants for membership to a soon-to-be affiliated Eagles Club or Region, and additional members of duly affiliated Eagles Club or Region in good standing. It shall be primarily given by PEIL through any its Director or to Regional Orientation Seminar Institute (ROSEI)
Director, duly authorized by the EPD.
1. In Eagles Region where there is a qualified ROSEI Director, the ORIENTS shall be conducted by ROSEI headed by and under the direct supervision of a PEIL Director assigned to the Region. The ROSEI Director shall be assisted by trainors duly appointed and designated by PEIL after having undergone the requisite day-long and live-in LEADS and other seminars.
2. The appointment and designation of trainors may be withdrawn or revoked by PEIL at any time after prior consultations with the ROSEI Director.
3. Request for ORIENTS addressed to ROSEI Director or Regional Governor shall be coordinated with PEIL which shall authorize the ROSEI Director or PEIL Director to hold the ORIENTS after prior compliance with prerequisites of ORIENTS as provided in the succeeding paragraph hereof.
4. ORIENTS; how and when given. Request for ORIENTS shall be addressed to the EPD who shall immediately advise

--- Page 133 ---
and coordinate with the National President, Secretary General or Regional Governor and ROSEI Director relative to the giving and holding of ORIENTS.
5. ORIENTS shall not be given unless the application for required fee shall be first submitted to the PEIL through its EPD or through ROSEI if the request shall have been addressed to it.
6. No ORIENTS shall be conducted or given unless the new applicants for membership shall have settled first the required national and regional dues, and affiliation fees to the Philippine Eagles.
7. Unless increased by PEIL, the existing seminar, fees and expenses as prescribed by the Philippine Eagles and paid by each applicant shall be remitted to PEIL as the applicant shall be advised accordingly. Upon recommendation of PEIL, the said current fee, may be increased by the National Assembly on a case to case basis, taking into account consumer price index, inflation and magnitude of seminars and teachings.
8. Other MANDATES expenses such as meals, hotel accommodation and transportation expenses shall be defrayed by the sponsoring Eagles Club or Eagles Region as the case may be.
9. ORIENTS Certificate. PEIL shall issue ORIENTS Certificate to the participants who shall have attended and duly completed the requisite ORIENTS in PE form which shall be prescribed and prepared by PEIL.
b. LEADS; by whom and to whom given objectives. The Leadership Seminar or LEADS shall be given solely and exclusively by PEIL Directors. The seminar curriculum the duration of which shall be prescribed by PEIL. It shall be given as a qualifying seminar for those Eagle-members intending

--- Page 134 ---
to be elected or appointed to any of the positions in the Eagles Clubs, Regions or national position in the Philippine Eagles as its frontline leaders, and executives; Members of the National Assembly, regional officers, and officers of the Committees and Commissions as prescribed hereof.
LEADS shall be a pre-condition to be elected or appointed to any national or regional positions in the Philippine Eagles.
Leadership seminars for national or regional positions shall be prescribed by PEIL.
PEIL shall issue Certificates of Leadership Completion to those who have taken and completed the LEADS.
c. NOSE; by whom and to whom given; objectives. - The National Officer’s Seminar or NOSE is solely and exclusively given by PEIL Directors. It is primarily designed for the incumbent elective and appointive national officers of the Philippine Eagles to enhance and improve their knowledge, among others: a) on their responsibilities, duties and functions relative to their positions; b) to the proposed programs and projects of the National President; and c)
proper implementation and compliance with the provisions of the Philippine Eagles Constitution and National Assembly Acts.
The NOSE shall be given not later than January 15 of each year following the elections and appointments of the national officers or before the Philippine Eagles inductions of the national officers if the NOSE may not be held earlier. If needed, NOSE may be given not later than June 30 of every year for those national officers who have not undergone NOSE. The NOSE curriculum shall be prescribed by PEIL.
d. SAVES; by whom and to whom given; objectives. - Spiritual Awareness and Values Education Seminar (SAVES) shall be solely and exclusively given by PEIL Directors. It is a priority designed for all Eagle-members to strengthen the spiritual

--- Page 135 ---
foundation of each Eagle-member into becoming a good, kind, humble, and strong Philipine Eagles that believes in the Universal Being, defender of people, saver of nature, and protector of our country.
e. Educational Information Campaign and Seminar on this Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024. - In order to cascade to all Eagle-members the provisions of the Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024, PEIL shall conduct the mandatory education information campaign and seminar on said constitution.
SECTION 10. Expenses for Seminars. Expenses for orientation seminars and other mandatory seminars to be conducted by the PEIL on Eagles Club or Region level shall be at the expense of the Eagle-Member attending said seminars.
SECTION 11. Seminars: Centralized Planning, Decentralized Execution.
The PEIL shall have a centralized and uniform system of conducting the MANDATES and related seminars throughout the Philippine Eagles.
However, any Eagles Region may be authorized to hold Eagles Club seminars upon prior authority from the PEIL and observance of the provisions of this Article.
The PEIL may authorize any Eagles Region to conduct Eagles Club seminars if there shall be competent and qualified seminar discussants in the Eagles Region.
SECTION 12. Seminar Discussants. Seminar discussants shall first undergo the MANDATES prescribed by the PEIL.
No Eagle-member may conduct Eagles Club seminars in any Region irrespective of the place he shall be from without the authority from the PEIL.
SECTION 13. Custody and Updating of Records. The PEIL shall keep all vital information and documents manually or electronically, pertaining to the Philippine Eagles and shall see to it that the information about the Philippine Eagles is updated.

articles.title: Philippine Eagles Commissions and Standing Committees
articles.summary: ARTICLE XI PHILIPPINE EAGLES COMMISSIONS AND SPECIAL EAGLES COMMISSIONS CHAPTER 1
articles.content:
--- Page 136 ---
ARTICLE XI
PHILIPPINE EAGLES COMMISSIONS AND
SPECIAL EAGLES COMMISSIONS
CHAPTER 1
PHILIPPINE EAGLES COMMISSIONS
SECTION 1. Creation of Philippine Eagles Commissions. The Philippine Eagle Commissions (PECOM) created in this Article shall be the following:
a. Commission on Membership (COME)
b. Commission on Extension (COMEX)
c. Commission on Education (COED)
d. Commission on Community Service (COMSERV)
e. Commission on Personal Relations (COMPERSONAL)
f.

Commission on Awards and Recognition (CARE)

g. Philippine Eagles Sports Commission (PESportsCom)
h. Philippine Eagles Tourism Commission (Tourism Com)
SECTION 2. Commission on Membership (COME) - Shall: (a) Devise ways and means to keep and enhance strong brotherhood ties among the Eagles; Regions and Clubs and the Philippine Eagles; (b)
Prepare the National Primer; and (c) Coordinate with the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership on strong membership and leadership development program including appropriate trainings, education seminars and learning resource materials. The COME shall be headed by the Chairman of the Committee on Membership duly appointed in the National Assembly.
SECTION 3. Commission on Extension (COMEX) - Shall: (a) Encourage the formation and organization of new Eagles Region or Eagles Club; and (b) Propose the mechanics and procedure regarding formation

--- Page 137 ---
and organization of new Region or Eagles club in the Philippines and other countries or overseas.
SECTION 4. Commission on Education (COED) - Shall devise ways and means and shall formulate plans and programs towards promoting health research, scientific inquiries, education and social legislation and provide forum for their open discussion, which can be submitted to the appropriate bodies as advocacies of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 5. Commission on Community Service (COMSERV) - Shall:
(a) Formulate the plans and mechanics of the Philippine Eagles for community service; (b) Devise ways and means to tap available resources that shall immediately promote and enhance the community service of the Philippine Eagles; and (e) Coordinate with Eagles Club and engage them in the task of community projects which shall have promoted and enhanced the prestige of the Philippine Eagles Regions and Clubs.
SECTION 6. Commission on Personal Relations (COMPERSONAL) Shall formulate plans and programs that shall facilitate exchange of business, professional, cultural, social and other opportunities for the mutual benefits of the Eagles and their Region and Eagles Club, in particular and the Philippine Eagles, in general.
SECTION 7. Commission on Awards and Recognition (CARE) - Shall:
(a) Prepare the rules, guidelines and criteria which shall institutionalize awards in the Philippine Eagles; and (b) Be the sole judge of the recipients of such institutional awards as catalogued in this Philippine Eagles Constitution. This Commission shall be headed by the National President as Chair and an appointive CARE Co-Chairman, to be appointed by the National President, and with the Executive National Vice-President, Vice Presidents for Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, Secretary General and the Chairman of the National Alalayang Agila as members thereof.

--- Page 138 ---
SECTION 8. Philippine Eagles Sports Commission (PESportsCom) Shall conduct sports tournament, games and other related events in the Philippine Eagles geared toward strengthening bonding and camaraderie among fellow-eagles and to promote physical activities and health to Eagle-members.
SECTION 9. Philippine Eagles Tourism Commission (Tourism Com) - Shall promote our country as tourists destination, enhance the cultural and heritage values of Philippine Eagles, and help in the advertisement campaign of tourism sites, places, and tourism enterprises owned and operated by Eagle-members.
SECTION 10. Categories of Philippine Eagles Awards. The categories of institutional awards in the Philippine Eagles shall be the following:
a. Philippine Eagles Outstanding Leadership Award (PEOLA)
b. Philippine Eagles Outstanding Service Award (PEOSA)
c. Philippine Eagles Loyalty Award (PELOYAL)
d. Philippine Eagles National Assembly Award (PENA)
e. Philippine Eagles National President’s Award (PREXY)
f.

Philippine Eagles (PENAPLE)

National

Presidents’

League

Award

g. Philippine Eagles Charter National President’s Award (PEACH)
h. Model Eagles Club of the Year Award (MECYA)
i.

Commission on Awards and Recognition (CARE)

j.

Model Eagles Region of the Year Award (MERYA)

SECTION 11. Philippine Eagles Outstanding Leadership Award (PEOLA)
It is awarded to a bonafide Eagle, if he has served as a National Officer or as a Regional Governor or member of the National Assembly, or as Chairman or Commissioner of a Philippine Eagles Commission or Special Eagles Commission or as a Region or Club officer; and b)

--- Page 139 ---
Has rendered or achieved exceptional or exemplary service to the Philippine Eagles, to his Region or Eagles Club, or to the community or country in general which shall be officially authenticated by documents demanded by CARE.
SECTION 12. Philippine Eagles Outstanding Service Award (PEOSA)
- May be awarded to a bonafide Eagles Region or Eagles Club, any commission, standing committee or interim or ad hoc committee which shall have rendered exceptional service to the Philippine Eagles or shall have undertaken exceptional project that redound to the goodwill and added prestige to the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 13. Philippine Eagles Loyalty Award (PELOYAL) - Shall be awarded to any Eagle-member who shall have been a bonafide and an active Eagle for at least five (5) years on the date the award and who shall not have been a member of any other service or civic organization or shall have ceased as an active member thereof for at least five (5) years on the date of the award.
SECTION 14. Philippine Eagles National Assembly Award (PENA) Shall be awarded to any Eagle who shall (a) Have sponsored and contributed outstanding legislation to the Philippine Eagles; or (b)
Have significantly contributed in improving the image of the Philippine Eagles through outstanding award received from the government or the private sector in any of his fields of endeavor.
SECTION 15. Philippine Eagles National President’s Award (PREXY) Shall be the incumbent National President’s Award and shall be given to any Eagle, Lady Eagle, or non-Eagle benefactor who shall have significantly assisted in any manner the National President during his incumbency and exclusively determined by him.
SECTION 16. Philippine Eagles National Presidents’ League Award (PENAPLE) - Shall be awarded to the Model Eagles Club of the Year as or Model Region Award as the CARE shall have adjudged or to any Eagle-member exclusively determined by PENAPLE.

--- Page 140 ---
SECTION 17. Philippine Eagles Charter National President’s Award (PEACH) - Shall be awarded to bonafide Eagles Region or Club or bonafide Eagle who shall have sponsored the organization and chartering of a new Eagles Club corresponding to the current year when the award shall have been given.
SECTION 18. Model Eagles Club of the Year Award (MECYA) - Shall be awarded to any bonafide Eagles Club which shall: (a) Have maintained actively its bonafide membership in the Philippine Eagles for the last three (3) years preceding the award; (b) Have increased its bonafide membership during the current year when the award shall have been given; (c) Have paid and settled on time its membership obligation including the payment of Eagles Club dues and renewal fee; and (d)
Have filed on time its monthly Club Activities Report (CLAR), to the Regional Governor who has jurisdiction of said Eagles club.
SECTION 19. Commission on Awards and Recognition (CARE) - May give its own award to any Eagle-member, Eagles Region or Eagles Club, or non- Eagle benefactor as it shall exclusively determine and decide, that added to the prestige of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 20. Model Eagles Region of the Year Award (MERYA) - MERYA shall be awarded to any affiliated region which a) have maintained actively its bonafide members in the Philippine Eagles for the last three
(3) years preceding the award; b) have increased its bonafide members during the current year when the award shall have been given; c)
have paid and settled on time its membership obligation including the payment of Eagles Clubs due within the region’s jurisdiction as well as renewal fee; d) have filed on time its quarterly Region Activities Report (REAR) to the National Secretarial through the Secretary General.

--- Page 141 ---
CHAPTER 2
SPECIAL EAGLES COMMISSIONS
SECTION 1. Special Eagles Commissions. The Special Eagles Commissions (SPECOM) and integral part of the Philippine Eagles and created in this Philippine Eagles Constitution shall be the following:
a. Commission on the Protection and Conservation of the Philippine Eagle (EAGLES’ PROTECT)
b. Talakayang Agila Commission (TALAKAYAN)
c. Alalayang Agila Commission (ALALAYAN)
d. Triple D Commission (TRIPLE D)
e. Miss Philippine Eagles Commission (MISPHIL)
f.

Environmental Conservation Commission

g. Commission on Senior Citizens
h. Dugong Agila-Sagip Agila Commission SECTION 2. Commission on the Protection and Conservation of the Philippine Eagle (EAGLES’ PROTECT) - Shall prepare a comprehensive study and program towards protecting and conserving the Philippine Eagle and shall devise ways and means by which resources may be tapped and harnessed to attain the objective through strong coordination with the government agencies and non-government agencies concerned and encourage all affiliated regions and clubs of the Philippine Eagles to achieve this purpose.
SECTION 3. Talakayang Agila Commission (TALAKAYAN) - Shall be an informal meeting and gathering of Eagles who shall meet regularly and spontaneously to the end that strong brotherhood, healthy fellowship and intense camaraderie among them shall be achieved.
The Talakayan may also be an occasion to discuss mutual opportunities beneficial to the Eagles, their Regions or Clubs, in particular and the Philippine Eagles in general.

--- Page 142 ---
SECTION 4. Alalayang Agila Commission (ALALAYAN) - General Concept.
Alalayang Agila shall means “Inter-supportive Eagles“ but shall transcend the mere supportive sense of helping a brother Eagle. It shall mean reliability of the Eagles commitment to a brother Eagle but shall never be taken as an attempt to dominate the person of the Eagle -member being meantime helped or assisted. The National Alalayang Agila Commission shall devise projects and programs to help the needy and other marginalized sector in order to uphold the objectives and purposes of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 5. ALALAYAN; Inter- Region and Eagles Club Relations. The ALALAYAN may be carried and extended to inter- Region and Eagles Club relationship. Regions or Eagles Clubs which share common or mutual interests may undertake any joint undertaking or project of common interest to the Regions or Eagles Clubs as determined and the undertaking shall have been initiated as if by only one Region or Eagles Club. In such Alalayan, the members shall have shared each other’s problems or moments of importance and shall have expanded and enhanced their sense and spirit of brotherhood.
SECTION 6. ALALAYAN - Shall devise ways and means by which the Alalayang Agila shall be evolved and institutionalized as a distinct Eagles culture and as a vehicle to attain strong and intense brotherhood between or among the Alalayan proponents.
SECTION 7. Triple D Commission (TRIPLE D) - Which shall mean “Disaster Donation Databank” of the Philippine Eagles, shall devise ways and means by which the databank service may be institutionalized and rendered effective and efficient. Triple D shall: (a) Maintain a databank which shall continually source the pledges of goods from the Eaglemembers; (b) Determine which of the pledges shall be called and the means by which donations shall be coursed through; (c) Coordinate, pick up and accept the physical goods donated; (d) Ensure that the donated goods shall have reached the intended beneficiaries; (e)
Secure pledges from goods consumed; (f) Make periodic reports on

--- Page 143 ---
the above activities; and (g) Maintain a well-organized public relations campaign about the service.
SECTION 8. Miss Philippine Eagles Commission (MISPHILCOM) - Shall be responsible in the selection of the Miss Philippine Eagles as, far as practicable. The Miss Philippine Eagles, as Ambassadress of Goodwill, may raise awareness of the goals and objectives of TFOE-PE. Inc. and prestige of the Philippine Eagles. The MISPHILCOM shall devise ways and means to professionalize such selection and the criteria.
SECTION 9. Environmental Conservation Commission - Shall devise ways and means to inculcate to Philippine Eagles “MAKA-KALIKASAN” and environmentalism to one’s individual, It shall develop programs and activities to Eagle-members as savers of Mother Earth and protectors of the Philippine nature.
SECTION 10. Philippine Eagles Senior Citizens Commission - Shall devise ways and means to provide additional rights and privileges to Eagle-members who have attained senior citizen and have been Eagle-members for at least ten (10) consecutive Eagle Year and in good standing. The Chairman of this Special Eagles Commission shall prescribe guidelines in closed coordination with Membership Committee, on Lifetime Membership and other privileges of senior citizens and such guidelines will be given priority by the National Assembly.
SECTION 11. Dugong Agila-Sagip Agila Commission - Shall coordinate in all levels the blood letting program of the Philippine Eagles.

--- Page 144 ---
CHAPTER 3
COMMON PROVISIONS
SECTION 1. Commissions; Composition; Term of Office. Each of the Commissions created under Chapters I and 2 of this Article except CARE shall be composed of a Chairman and at least two Commissioners to be appointed by the National President. The appointment of the Chairman and Commissioners shall be confirmed by the Appointments Commission (APCOM).
The Chairman or the Commissioners shall serve for a term of one (1)
year from date of their respective written appointments, but in no case shall be beyond the term of the appointing National President.
SECTION 2. Reportorial Requirements. Each of the Commission created under Chapters 1 and 2 of this Article shall submit a quarterly report to the National President through the Secretary General, either manually or electronically, copy furnished the National Assembly through the National Assembly Secretary or Chairman of the Rules and Constitutional Amendments Committee.

articles.title: Philippine Eagles Accounting and Audit
articles.summary: ARTICLE XII PHILIPPINE EAGLES ACCOUNTING AND AUDIT CHAPTER 1 PHILIPPINE EAGLES ACCOUNTING
articles.content:
--- Page 145 ---
ARTICLE XII
PHILIPPINE EAGLES ACCOUNTING AND AUDIT
CHAPTER 1
PHILIPPINE EAGLES ACCOUNTING
SECTION 1. Title. This Article shall be known and cited as the Philippine Eagles Accounting and Audit Act.
SECTION 2. Applicability. This Article shall be applicable to all levels, bodies, Commissions or other bodies of the Philippine Eagles wherever budget or funds for their operations shall be allocated, alloted, disbursed or named in their respective account. All checks of the Philippine Eagles shall have and carry at least two (2) signatories one of which shall be that of the National President and co-signed either by the National Treasurer or any other National Officer or member of the Board of Trustees duly authorized for that purpose. In the absence of the National President, an alternate co-signatory preferably the Executive National Vice President (ENVP) may be designated for the duration of the absence of the National President.
SECTION 3. Payment, Orders, Cash Vouchers. Payment orders or cash vouchers shall have and carry the signature of the National Treasurer and shall be approved by the National President with supporting documents, reviewed by the national officer’s concerned.
The vouchers shall be numerically and chronologically numbered for auditing purpose.
SECTION 4. Petty Cash. A petty cash fund shall be established in the amount to be determined by the National President taking into account consumer price index and inflation and the usual needs of the Philippine Eagles.
The said petty cash shall be applicable to the following expenditures, to be determined by the National President, the amount of which

--- Page 146 ---
shall take into account consumer price index and inflation, subject to the review and approval of the National Assembly and every 3 years thereafter, to wit:
a. Office supplies such as ink, pencils, ball pens, stationeries, envelopes, film and other similar items;
b. Communication expenses which shall include postages, telegrams, cablegrams, toll fees, stamps, telephone calls and other similar expenses;
c. Other expenses shall include reproduction or photocopying of documents and needed materials; and
d. Other supplies needed by the national office for meetings and representation, including the necessary transportation expenses.
SECTION 5. Supporting Documents on Expenditures. Expenditures incurred shall be supported by receipts and other supporting documents as required and shall be signed by the person availing of the petty cash and counter signed by the National Treasurer.
SECTION 6. Liquidation of Cash Advances. Cash advances shall be liquidated within fifteen (15) days from completion of the activity, event or program in which the same shall have been incurred.
SECTION 7. Accounting Procedure. The Finance Secretary, in coordination with the National Treasurer, shall prescribe the Philippine Eagles accounting procedure based on accepted accounting principle, rules and regulations and good governance as prescribed by SEC on non-stock corporation.
SECTION 8. Maintenance of Journal and Ledger.
a. The National Treasurer shall see to it that a general journal, membership ledger and expense ledger be maintained separately and shall be officials of the Philippine Eagles for review, during office hours and at reasonable time.

--- Page 147 ---
b. The Finance Secretary shall prepare and prescribe the internal control system and submit quarterly report to the National President copy furnish the National Assembly through the National Assembly Secretary and the Auditor General.
c. All other commissions, other bodies and in all levels of the TFOE-PE. Inc. shall likewise prepare a general journal membership and expense ledgers, separately.
SECTION 9. Books of Account. The Philippine Eagles shall keep Books of Accounts which shall be audited internally but may be audited externally based on the policy to be determined by the National Assembly and Board of Trustees, as the case may be.
Said books shall be as follows:
a. Salaries and allowances
b. Office supplies and the likes
c. Rental expense, other fees and maintenance
d. Telephone and communication expenses like internet connections
e. Electricity and water bills f.

Similar communication expense such as postage and freight

g. Transportation and traveling expenses
h. Food and drinks i.

Repairs and maintenance

j.

Donations and contributions

k. Eagles Forum, Souvenir Programs and Certificates l.

Expenses for National Assembly, National Congress, meetings and authorized activities

m. Other Miscellaneous Expenses as prescribed.

--- Page 148 ---
CHAPTER 2
AUDIT SECTION 1. Auditor General. The Auditor General shall be appointed by the National President subject to confirmation by the Appointments Commission (APCOM). The Auditor General shall be preferably at least a Certified Public Accountant or has experience in audit.
SECTION 2. Not a Member of Cabinet. The Auditor General shall not be a member of the Administration of the National President and his position shall be as independent as possible from the Executive, National Assembly and Supreme Tribunal of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 3. Duties. The Auditor General shall pass in audit disbursements and expenditures of the Philippine Eagles and shall have such their duties and functions as shall be inherent or incidental to his position.
SECTION 4. Auditing Procedure. The Auditor General shall prescribe a standard auditing procedure in the Philippine Eagles based on accepted audit practices, rules and regulatory and must see to it that other commissions, and inferior bodies should comply to the standard auditing procedure.
The auditing procedure shall be in a way as shall achieve the following:
a. Serve as basis to express an opinion as to the fairness and consistency of the Philippine Eagles financial statement;
b. Discover errors in the financial report;
c. Serve as a basis for proposing changes in the existing accounting practice and operational procedure of the Philippine Eagles; and
d. Show the general financial stewardship of the Philippine Eagles.

--- Page 149 ---
CHAPTER 3
REPORT SECTION 1. Report. The Auditor General shall prepare a quarterly Report on the audit of the funds and disbursements thereof of the Philippine Eagles, the Executive, Natural Assembly, and Supreme Tribunal, the commissions and other inferior bodies.
SECTION 2. Report submission. The report shall be submitted to the National President through the Secretary General, copy furnish the National Assembly through the National Assembly Secretary or the Chairman of the Rules and Constitutional Amendment Committee, as the case may be.

--- Page 150 ---
ARTICLE XIII
SEAL, EMBLEM, OR LOGO, GONG AND GAVEL,
EAGLES MACE, OFFICIAL NAME AND LETTERHEAD,
PINS, UNIFORMS, IDENTIFICATION CARDS, BANNERS,
AND PHILIPPINE EAGLES SPECIMEN
CHAPTER 1
SEAL, EMBLEM, OR LOGO, GONG AND GAVEL,
EAGLES MACE, OFFICIAL NAME AND LETTERHEAD,
PINS, UNIFORMS, IDENTIFICATION CARDS, BANNERS
AND PHILIPPINE EAGLE SPECIMEN
SECTION 1. Seal, Emblem, or Logo. The seal, emblem or logo of the Philippine Eagles shall be circular in form and shall bear the existing emblem or logo and shall be in size and measurement as prescribed herein and adopted by the National Assembly.
SECTION 2. DEO ET PATRIA. -The words DEO ET PATRIA shall be bannered as the additional principle of the Philippine Eagles and shall be added and printed below the official logo of the Philippine Eagles as integral part thereof.
As so added and printed in the Philippine Eagles logo, the word DEO shall mean for GOD while the word PATRIA shall mean FOR COUNTRY.
The Emblem or Logo of the Philippine Eagles is hereto reproduced and shown for the guidance and reference of all Eagle-members.

--- Page 151 ---
The Certificate of Registration of said logo or emblem was given by the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPO Phil) under Certificate of Registration No. 4/2023/00524317, duly registered on March 4, 2024 with 10 years term or until March 4, 2034.
SECTION 3. Evolution of the Philippines Eagles Seal, Emblem or Logo.
The Philippine Eagles logo may be evolved and improved from time to time but the same shall be done once every ten (10) years. Any proposed new logo shall be approved by the National Assembly.
For historical record, the Philippine Eagles seal, emblem or logo has evolved since 1979, duly adopted by the National Assembly as shown:

SECTION 4. Gong and Gavel. The Gong and Gavel shall be the symbol of official authority, leadership and responsibility in the Philippine Eagles and shall be consistently availed during its official meetings, formal affairs or occasions, in national, regions or Eagles Club and shall be properly placed at the center of the table where the Presiding Officer shall be seated.
Unless officially changed or modified, the design of the Gong and Gavel duly approved by then General Assembly 7 7

National Assembly

--- Page 152 ---
in 1982, (now National Assembly) shall remain in full force and effect and shall be consistently used by the Philippine Eagles, regions, Eagles clubs which shall not deviate there from by using unofficial Gong and Gavel.
The gong and gavel shall be treated with respect and shall not be placed in the floor or in an inappropriate manner.
SECTION 5. Sizes of Gong and Gavel. The sizes of the Philippine Eagles Going and Gavel shall be catalogued as big, medium and small.
The big size shall be used exclusively by a) the incumbent National President, b) PENAPLE. It is called the Philippine Eagles National Gong and Gavel; the medium size by the Eagles Regions and other National Officers, committees, commissions and bodies; and the small size, by the Eagles Club.
The sizes of gong and gavel shall conform to the following dimensions:
a. National Gong and Gavel

--- Page 153 ---
b. Regional, Gong and Gavel and other National Officers committees, commissions and bodies

REGIONAL AND OTHER NATIONAL
OFFICERS GONG AND GAVEL

c. Eagles Club

EAGLES CLUB AND GONG GAVEL

--- Page 154 ---
SECTION 6. The Philippine Eagles Mace. The Philippine Eagles shall adopt a Philippine Eagles Mace as the symbol of authority of the Sergeant-at-Arms in the National Assembly or by the Regions and Eagles Clubs Protocol Officers in maintaining peace and order. The sizes shall be in accordance on the gong and gavel as large, medium and small.

EAGLES MACE

18 inches, Large National or 45 cm 15 inches, Medium Region or 37.5 cm 12 inches, Small Eagles or Club 30 cm SECTION 7. The Philippine Eagles Charter Grant. The Philippine Eagles Charter Grant shall be granted to Region or Eagles Club who is applying to be duly affiliated to the Philippine Eagles. The charter grant shall conform to PE Form 1 as prescribed in Eagles Forms as provided in Article XVIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
The Charter Grant shall be in conformity with the provisions of Sections 8, 9, 10, and 11, Chapter 3, Article IX of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 8. Official Name and Letterhead. The official name of the Philippine Eagles shall be, The Fraternal Order of Eagles - Philippine Eagles, Inc. and shall remain in full force and effect. It shall also be briefly called the Philippine Eagles.
Unless otherwise changed or modified, the official letterhead of the Philippine Eagles, as well as the existing emblem or logo, its color scheme or combination thereof, shall remain in full force and effect and shall consistently be observed and followed.
The official letterhead of the Philippine Eagles shall and maintain the pictorial representation of its official emblem which shall be printed on the right side thereof and the pictorial representation of the Philippine Flag which shall be printed on its left side as officially

--- Page 155 ---
sanctioned by the continuous practices and traditions of the Philippine Eagles since its founding in 1979 and shall remain in full force and effect, as follows:

SECTION 9. Pins. Unless modified by the National Assembly, the official pin of the Philippine Eagles shall be consistent with the Eagles emblem, seal, or logo as shown below:

The official pin of the Philippine Eagles may be changed or modified by the National President and subject to review and approval by the National Assembly but must conform with the official seal, emblem or logo.
SECTION 10. Uniforms.
a. The uniform of the Members of the National Assembly shall be decided by the National Assembly which may create a Uniform Committee for said purpose.
b. The uniform of the Executive National Officers shall be decided by the National President or by the Board of Trustees.

--- Page 156 ---
c. Regional and Eagles Club uniforms shall be decided by the Eagles Region or Eagles Club, as the case may be.
d. National officers uniforms shall be designed in accordance with the positions they hold.
e. To have uniformity and unity, it is encouraged to have one color of uniforms for the Philippine Eagles. The National President shall issue directive for its proper implementation.
SECTION 11. Identification Card. The Philippine Eagles identification card shall be in text, form, size and design prescribed in PE Form 11, Article XVIII, hereof.
SECTION 12. Philippine Eagles Banner. The existing banner of the Philippine Eagles shall be maintained and shall be in size, measurement, color and description as prescribed herein. The official color shall be Beige and to be provided in its perimeter with Brown four inches Tassel, unless prescribed by the National Assembly. No deviation as to the color of the Philippine Eagles banner is allowed.

The National Banner shall be displayed at the podium.
SECTION 13. Regional Banner. Every Eagles Region shall have a banner in form, size, measurement and pattern as prescribed herein and in conformity with the Philippine Eagles Banner.

--- Page 157 ---
a. The Regional Banner shall be identical in form, shape and color with the National Banner except in size.
b. The Regional Horizontal Banner shall be displayed at the podium.

The Horizontal banner shall be back to back using the logo.
SECTION 14. Eagles Club Banner. The Eagles Club banner shall be in form, size, measurement and pattern as prescribed herein and in conformity with Philippine Eagles banner.

--- Page 158 ---
SECTION 15. Display of Banner. The banners shall be ready and available for appropriate display during the affairs of the Philippine Eagles, Regions or Eagles Clubs and other activities or programs as prescribed by the National Assembly.
SECTION 16. Production of Eagles Paraphernalia. The herein mentioned Philippine Eagles paraphernalia such as Charter Grant, Pins, Mace, Banners, Gong & Gavel shall be produced by duly accredited entity or manufacturer as prescribed by the National President.
SECTION 17. The Philippine Eagle Specimen. The Philippine eagle specimen donated by the Lifetime Honorary National President shall, if warranted, and as far as practicable be conspicuously displayed during the formal affairs or occasions of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 18. The Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024. The original copy of the Philippine Eagle Constitution of 2024, duly signed by the twenty-nine (29) Commissioners of the Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024 shall be preserved and displayed during the Philippine Eagles Week.
CHAPTER 2
PROGRAM AND PROTOCOL PROGRAM
SECTION 1. The Philippine Eagles Program. The Philippine Eagles Program shall refer to the system of precedence or plan of procedure to be observed and followed during official and formal affairs or occasions of the Philippine Eagles, the Regions or Eagles Clubs affiliated with the TFOE-PE, Inc. including the commissions and other bodies.

--- Page 159 ---
SECTION 2. The invitation. The invitation of the Philippine Eagles shall substantially observe the following format:

THE FRATERNAL ORDER OF Eagles - Philippine Eagles, Inc.
(Official script design of the word Eagles shall be observed)
Cordially invites you to its (State nature of occasion)
to be held on (State date and time)
at the (State the place)
____________________________________________ ____________________________________________ Attire: (state the kind of attire)
Philippine Eagles: “FIRST PHILIPPINE-BORN FRATERNAL SOCIO-CIVIC
ORGANIZATION”

SECTION 3. The Philippine Eagles Program format. The Philippine Eagles Program format shall be substantially followed during formal affairs or occasions of the Philippine Eagles, the Regions and Eagles Clubs, Commissions and Other Bodies, unless otherwise prescribed by the National Assembly upon the recommendations of PEIL or PENAPLE.
SECTION 4. The Philippine Eagles Programme. The Philippine Eagle programme format shall be substantially observed and followed during inductions, chartering of other formal occasions of the eagles, all regions and clubs.

--- Page 160 ---
SECTION 5. The Program Format. The following Programme format shall be substantially followed:
PROGRAMME Registration &Cocktail (state time)
Call to Order Entry of Mace Entry of Colors Eagle Universal Prayer Pambansang Awit Philippine Eagles Hymn Welcome /Opening Remarks Acknowledgment & Introduction of Guests and Eagles Eagles Pledge (One intermission number may follow, if desired)
Dinner &Intermission Number (If applicable)
Induction Ceremonies (state below who shall be inducted)
National President’s Address, or National Officers or Regional Governor address, in case of the absence of the National President or National Officer Introduction of Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS)
(If applicable)

(If applicable)
Eagles Toast Awarding Ceremonies Eagles Impromptu Hour or Fellowship (If desired, but shall be done after the GOHAS shall have left)
Closing Remarks Exit of Colors Adjournment

--- Page 161 ---
SECTION 6. Other items in the Program. Other items may be included in the program provided the same shall not substantially deviate from the basic format as provided above.
SECTION 7. Mandate or Brush Script. Whenever the name of The Fraternal Order of Eagles - Philippine Eagles, Inc. shall appear in the program or invitation, be it in the national, or regional, or club level, the official script letter form of the word “Eagles“, in Brush Script font style shall be followed.
CHAPTER 3
PHILIPPINE EAGLES PROTOCOL
SECTION 1. The Philippine Eagles Protocol shall refer to the set of rules of etiquette or ceremony to be observed and followed by the Philippine Eagles during its official and formal affairs or occasions or similar events and activities.
SECTION 2. The Philippine Eagles Protocol shall be continuously evolved and developed provided it shall not deviate from well established and accepted protocol practices, procedure and precedents. The Philippine Eagles Protocol shall be reviewed by the PENAPLE and PEIL, who will make recommendations and changes, if any.
SECTION 3. During official and formal affairs or occasions or similar events and activities of the Philippine Eagles, all regions or clubs.
The Eagles Protocol shall be observed and followed substantially.
SECTION 4. The Eagles Protocol shall cover the following subject matters:
a. Official Name and Letterhead
b. Gong and Gavel
c. Philippine Eagles Mace

--- Page 162 ---
d. Philippine Eagles Program
e. Philippine Eagles Time f.

Entry of Colors, Proper Display of the Philippine Flag, Philippine Eagles Banner, Regional and Eagles Club Banners

g. Reception and Escorting of Guests
h. Seating Arrangements i.

Master of Ceremonies

j.

Rules of Introduction

k. Philippine Eagles Fraternal Greetings and Recognized Practices and Traditions l.

Turnover Rites

m. Philippine Eagles Universal Prayer
n. Philippine Eagles Pledge
o. Philippine Eagles Toast
p. Philippine Eagles Welcome, Opening, and Closing Remarks
q. Introduction of Past National Presidents
r. Intermission Numbers or Entertainment SECTION 5. The provisions of Chapter 1 of this Article shall be deemed part of the Philippine Eagles Protocol.
SECTION 6. Philippine Eagles Time. The Philippine Eagles Time shall be the punctual time and on time. The Philippine Eagles shall observe and follow the Philippine Eagles Time at all times while and when attending the meetings, affairs or occasions of the Philippine Eagles, its regions, clubs, committees, commissions and other bodies.
Eagle-Members and other participants in the Philippine Eagles meetings, affairs, occasions shall specially observe the Philippine Eagles Time which is punctual and on time.

--- Page 163 ---
SECTION 7. Entry of Colors
a. The entry of colors shall observe and follow the existing practice or tradition of the Philippine Military, Police or Other Uniformed Personnel, if practicable.
b. The Philippine Flag shall be displayed properly during the Philippine Eagles meetings, affairs and other appropriate occasions.
c. The Philippine Eagles banner, the regional banners or the Eagles club banners, shall be appropriately displayed at the left side of the stage facing the audience during the affairs or occasions of the Philippine Eagles where such display may be required following existing practices or traditions or precedents.
SECTION 8. Reception and Escorting of Guests. Upon his arrival, the special Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS) shall be properly and immediately escorted to his assigned seat at the presidential table.
The arrival of GOHAS shall signal the immediate commencement of the Philippine Eagles Program.
Other guests with assigned seats in the presidential or secondary presidential table shall be appropriately and similarly escorted by the Philippine Eagles Protocol Officer or to any such place where they shall be properly seated, as far as practicable.
SECTION 9. Philippine Eagles Seating Arrangement. The Philippine Eagles seating arrangements in the presidential table or secondary presidential table shall be appropriately attended to and decided by the Philippine Eagles Protocol Officer in coordination with the National Officer, Regional Officer or Eagles Club Officer as the case may be.
SECTION 10. Master of Ceremonies. The Master of Ceremonies shall see to it that the Philippine Eagles Program shall be followed and shall adhere to the accepted rules, practices or traditions and precedents

--- Page 164 ---
as to the correct conduct and decorum of a master of ceremonies and flow of the Programme.
No Eagle-member shall qualify as a Master of Ceremonies unless he shall have been properly oriented about the Philippine Eagles Program and Protocols. It shall be the responsibility of the Philippine Eagles Protocol Officer to provide proper orientation to the Master of Ceremonies on matters about the Philippine Eagles Program.
The Master of Ceremonies shall avoid making unguarded and inappropriate adlib including other unnecessary and offensive remarks.
SECTION 11. Rules of Introduction. The Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS) shall be appropriately introduced by following the accepted practices or traditions.
No Eagle-member shall accept the responsibility of introducing the Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS), who is unprepared to handle the job. The Philippine Eagles Protocol Officer shall politely provide guidance to the Philippine Eagle doing the introduction on the appropriate rules to introduce a Guest of Honor and Speaker (GOHAS) and must see to it that he is willing and capable.
SECTION 12. Late Coming to the Philippine Eagles Affair is Discouraged.
Late-coming to the Philippine Eagles affair or occasion shall be discouraged. After the introduction and acknowledgment of the guests and Eagles in attendance as prescribed in the Philippine Eagles Program, the introduction of the Eagle late-comer or any guest shall be a matter of option and not of obligation on the part of the master of ceremonies. No dramatic introduction shall be made to the late-corner.
The announcement of the arrival of a late-comer shall not interrupt any on-going program or proceedings and shall be done appropriately with less emphasis on his late-coming after the completion of the ongoing number.

--- Page 165 ---
SECTION 13. Fraternal Greetings and Eagles Recognized Practices and Traditions.
a. During formal affairs or occasions, or events an Eagle shall be publicly greeted, addressed, or introduced in the following manner and examples: Eagle National President, Kuya ABC; Eagle Charter National President, Kuya Nilo Raymundo; Eagle National President, Kuya DEF; Eagle National Vice President or Eagle Regional Governor, Kuya GHI; Eagle National Secretary General, Kuya MNO; Eagles Club President, Kuya QRS; or the likes, and Kuya MNO and so on and so forth.
In non-formal meetings, gatherings, affairs, or occasions, all Eagle shall be addressed simply as Kuya or Ate, as the case maybe.
b. During formal affairs or occasions, the Lady Eagle: shall be greeted, addressed, or introduced in the following manner and examples: Lady Eagle First Lady, Ate XYZ; Lady Eagle, Club President, Ate TUV and the likes and so on and so forth.
In non-formal meetings, gatherings, affairs, or occasions, the Lady Eagle shall be addressed simply as Ate Mariel, Ate MGD and the likes and so on and so forth.
Rules of introduction of guests shall follow the accepted practices or traditions on the subject substantially.
CHAPTER 4
PHILIPPINE EAGLES INSTITUTIONAL PRACTICES
SECTION 1. Recognized Practices. The Philippine Eagles shall adhere, as part of its evolving culture and tradition to the Philippine Eagles Brotherhood Handshake and the Philippine Eagles Fraternal Greetings which shall call a brother Eagle, Kuya regardless of age, title, rank, or station in life, and a Lady Eagle, Ate.
SECTION 2. Turn-Over Rites. Turn-over ceremonies shall be formal and solemn. The outgoing National President and the incoming

--- Page 166 ---
National President shall see to it that the solemnity and formality of the turn-over be observed.
SECTION 3. Turn-Over of Gong and Gavel. The outgoing National President shall turnover the Gong and Gavel to the incoming National President as symbolic of the turn-over of the authority, leadership and responsibility of the presidency from the former to the latter or other officers.
During the turn-over of the Gong and Gavel, the outgoing National President shall say, as follows:
“I hereby dutifully turn over this Gong and Gavel and faithfully yield unto you the authority, leadership and responsibility of the (state the position) of (state the Eagles Club, if appropriate) of (state the Region) of the Philippine Eagles.”

Upon acceptance of the Gong and Gavel, the incoming office shall say, as follows:
“I hereby whole-heartedly accept this Gong and Gavel as a symbol of my authority, leadership and responsibility as (state the position) of (state the Eagles Club) of (state the Region) of the Philippine Eagles for Eagle Year___________”

SECTION 4. Responsibility of the Protocol Officer. It shall be the responsibility of the Philippine Eagles Protocol Officer to see to it that the solemnity and formality of the turn-over rites shall be faithfully observed.
SECTION 5. Observance of the Turn-over Rites in All Regions, Eagles Clubs and Levels. This rule on turn-over rites shall be observed in all regions, Eagles clubs, commissions, committees and other bodies of the Philippine Eagles as prescribed above, with certain modifications on title and positions.

--- Page 167 ---
SECTION 6. The Philippine Eagle Universal Prayer. The Philippine Eagles Universal Prayer shall be recited as an invocation in all occasions, events, National Assembly, National Congress and meetings by the Philippine Eagles. It shall be preceded by the singing or playing of the Philippine National Anthem and Philippine Eagles Hymn.
SECTION 7. Philippine Eagles Pledge. The Philippine Eagles Pledge shall be recited during official and formal affairs or occasions or other events like general membership meeting, regional assembly, regional executive meeting of the Philippine Eagles, in all regions or Eagles Clubs. It shall may be included as part of the program of any other Eagles meeting or activities.
SECTION 8. Philippine Eagles Toast. Formal Philippine Eagles Toast shall be included in the formal, affairs occasions or meetings of the Philippine Eagles, all regions, and clubs, commissions and other inferior bodies.
SECTION 9. The Philippine Eagles Welcome Remarks. The Philippine Eagle welcome remarks shall be brief and appropriate, following accepted practices or traditions.
SECTION 10. The Philippine Eagles Opening Remarks. The opening remarks shall be appropriate and relevant to the affair or occasion and must be brief and concise.
SECTION 11. The Philippine Eagles Closing Remarks. The closing remarks shall be concise and appropriate following accepted practices or traditions.
SECTION 12. The Philippine Eagles Inspirational Message. The Philippine Eagle Inspirational message or any Eagle fraternal message shall be relevant to the occasion affairs or meetings and shall be time framed for a period reasonable and must not be too long.

--- Page 168 ---
SECTION 13. Intermission or Entertainment Numbers. Intermission or entertainment numbers shall be time framed in such a way that they shall not imperil the order or distract the Philippine Eagles Program.
SECTION 14. Protocol Governing Past National Presidents. As a matter of practice and policy, only the incumbent National President and his Lady Eagle and the Immediate Past National President shall not pre-empt sitting in the presidential or head table.
Past National Presidents and their respective Lady Eagles may be given assigned seats as near the presidential or secondary presidential table as far as practicable. In no case shall they be seated at the secondary presidential table which shall be reserved to other incumbent National Officers Regional Governors and Eagles Club Presidents.
Past National Presidents shall be requested to seat at the presidential table on any available seat in whose favor the seats shall have been reserved as far as practicable. In such a case, the Past National President concerned shall not decline but shall take a sporting gesture to be seated at the presidential table. Vacant seat or seats shall be yielded to the Past National Presidents who shall have arrived first for the occasions, meetings, events or similar activities which arrival shall be conclusively ascertained by the Eagles Protocol Officer from the registration book or attendance sheet.
CHAPTER 5
OATHS, EAGLES PLEDGE, EAGLES MARCH, RITUALS
SECTION 1. Member’s Oath. The Eagles member’s oath shall be in PE Forms 5 of Article XVIII of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 2. Oath of Office, Club Officers. The oath of office of club officers shall adopt PE Form 6, Article XVIII, of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.

--- Page 169 ---
SECTION 3. Oath of Office, National Officers. The oath of office of the National Officers shall be provided in PE Form 7, Article XVIII, of this Philippine Eagles Constitution.
SECTION 4. Philippine Eagles Authorized to Administer Oaths. The National Presidents of the Philippine Eagles, incumbent and past, the incumbent Executive National Vice President, National Vice Presidents for Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao and Regional Governors as well as incumbent Supreme Chancellor and Secretary General of the Philippine Eagles shall have the general authority to administer oaths in the Philippine Eagles, as the case may be. In case of the Eagles Club, upon the authority of the Regional Governor, the incumbent Club President may have the authority to administer oath in his Eagles Club or to its officers.
SECTION 5. Philippine Eagles Pledge. The existing Philippine Eagles Pledge shall be retained with modifications and shall be, as follows:
PHILIPPINE Eagles PLEDGE “I, having consciously subscribed to the Philippine Eagles Constitution and the By-Laws, Rules and Regulations of the Philippine Eagles, and aware of my responsibility to my God and Country, do hereby pledge to promote and defend at all times said Eagles Constitution and By-Laws and their ideals to the best of my ability and within my power and capacity.
So, Help Me God.”

--- Page 170 ---
The translation in Filipino of the Philippine Eagles Pledge shall be, as follows:
PANUNUMPA NG AGILA
(PHILIPPINE EAGLES PLEDGE)
“Ako si, na buong katapatang susunod sa Saligang Batas ng Philippine Eagles, at mga batas at alituntunin nito, at aking tungkulin sa Panginoon at sa Bayan, ay nanunumpa na aking palalaganapin at ipagsasanggalang sa lahat ng panahon ang nabanggit na Saligang Batas at kalakip na batas at ang mga pamantayan at alintuntunin nito, sa abot ng aking talino, lakas at kakayahan.
Tulungan Nawa Ako ng Panginoon.”

SECTION 6. Philippine Eagles March. The Philippine Eagles March shall remain the official hymn of the Philippine Eagles and shall be as follow:

SECTION 7. Philippine Eagles Rituals. The Philippine Eagles shall evolve its, rituals which shall be prescribed by the Philippine Eagles Institute of Leadership (PEIL) and to be submitted to the National Assembly for consideration and approval.

articles.title: Philippine Eagles National Presidents
articles.summary: ARTICLE XIV PHILIPPINE EAGLES NATIONAL PRESIDENTS’ LEAGUE (PENAPLE) CHAPTER 1
articles.content:
--- Page 171 ---
ARTICLE XIV
PHILIPPINE EAGLES NATIONAL
PRESIDENTS’ LEAGUE (PENAPLE)
CHAPTER 1
PHILIPPINE EAGLES NATIONAL PRESIDENTS’ LEAGUE
SECTION 1. There is hereby created the Philippine Eagles National Presidents’ League, hereafter referred to as the PENAPLE, which shall be composed of all Past National Presidents and the incumbent National President of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 2. Membership to the PENAPLE shall be exclusively limited to any Eagle-member who shall have served or is serving as National President of the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 3. The PENAPLE shall:
a. Be an official and highest advisory of the Philippine Eagles;
b. Be fully supportive of the programs of the Philippine Eagles;
c. Meet as regularly as possible;
d. Be continuously committed to support a sustained quality membership growth and programs of the Philippine Eagles;
e. Help devise plans and programs to achieve the institutional goals and objectives of the Philippine Eagles; f.

Help devise an effective and efficient management system to run the Philippine Eagles;

g. Attend the National Assembly and National Congress with voting right for each member of the PENAPLE; and
h. Adopt and promulgate its rules governing its meetings, elections of officers, if desired, conduct and discipline of its members.

--- Page 172 ---
SECTION 4. The PENAPLE shall be primarily supportive and shall not be pre-emptive of the leadership in the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 5. The National President may request to convene the PENAPLE from time to time for consultations and advice. The incumbent National President is an ex-officio member of the PENAPLE.
Taking into account their contributions to the growth and expansion of the Philippine Eagles, PENAPLE shall be provided with administrative and technical support during their attendance to the official functions and meetings of the Philippine Eagles, National Assembly and National Congress.
Any PENAPLE member may call a meeting thereof, but a majority of the members must attend in order to discharge the PENAPLE’S functions as provided herein.
In the conduct of the PENAPLE’s meeting or consultation as the case may be, administrative and financial support to be charged from the PENAPLE’S fund as appropriated by the Philippine Eagles shall be provided to the PENAPLE.
SECTION 6. Philippine Eagles National Presidents’ League (PENAPLE); Election and Term of Office of its Officers.
a. The PENAPLE shall elect by consensus its Chairman, ViceChairman, Secretary and Treasurer who shall serve for a term of two (2) years from their election. After the term of office of the PENAPLE Chairman, the Vice-Chairman shall automatically assume the position of the Chairman, if qualified and fit.
b. After the expiration of the term of office of the elected Chairman, the Vice Chairman, who was elected together with the Chairman, shall automatically assume the position of the Chairman, if qualified to serve for a term of two (2) years.
c. Thereafter, PENAPLE shall elect the new Vice-Chairman, Secretary and Treasurer, who shall serve for a term of two
(2) years from their election.

--- Page 173 ---
d. In case of vacancy in the office of the Chairman, due to resignation, death or incapacity, the Vice-Chairman shall discharge and perform the duties of the Chairman for the remaining term.
e. In case of the assumption into office of the Vice-Chairman as Chairman, the PENAPLE shall elect from among themselves the Vice-Chairman, Secretary and Treasurer.
f.

In order to have a smooth transition of officers, the provisions in paragraph (b) and (c) of this Section shall be observed.

SECTION 7. PENAPLE shall be as strong as credible as the Miranda and Credenda of Leadership in the Philippine Eagles. The PENAPLE shall always remain as strong and as credible at all times as the official advisory body of the Philippine Eagles. Any advice rendered shall maintain itself both as Miranda and Credenda of Leadership.
SECTION 8. PENAPLE Oversight Commission is hereby created. There is hereby created the PENAPLE Oversight Commission composed of the PENAPLE Chairman and four (4) other members who shall be appointed by the Chairman.
SECTION 9. PENAPLE Oversight Commission is equally an advisory body; referral of its advice to the proper body. - Complaints addressed to the PENAPLE shall be referred by the PENAPLE Oversight Commission to the appropriate body of the Philippine Eagles which may be tasked to act on the complaint. The written referral shall contain its official advice regarding any complaint brought to it which may be heeded or not by the body to which the written advice may be referred to.
Written complaint addressed to the PENAPLE Oversight Commission against any elected national officer of the Philippine Eagles shall be referred to the National Assembly for prompt and appropriate action while written complaint against any national officer appointed to any national position shall be referred to the National President for appropriate and proper action. In either case, the written advice of the PENAPLE shall be attached to the referral.

--- Page 174 ---
The National Assembly or the National President, as the case may be, shall resolve the complaint referred to either by the PENAPLE Oversight Commission within sixty (60) days from receipt of the referral.
SECTION 10. Delegate Authority to any PENAPLE Member. Upon the authority of the incumbent National President, any member of the PENAPLE may exercise the following duties and functions:
a. To preside the Chartering and Oath of Affiliation of Charter Members or Officers of soon to be chartered Eagles Club or Region;
b. To preside the Oath of Affiliation of Additional Members or Oath of Office of Affiliated Eagles Club or Region: and
c. To perform such other matters as may be delegated to any member of PENAPLE or to PENAPLE as a collegial body, including appointment to any Philippine Eagles committee, commissions, tribunals or similar bodies, where their advice and expertise are needed.
SECTION 11. PENAPLE’S Integrity, Probity and Dignity Beyond Reproach.
As members of PENAPLE, each member shall be of Eagle-member with integrity, probity and dignity beyond reproach, and is immune from administrative complaint.

articles.title: Philippine Eagles Code of Conduct & Fraternal Discipline
articles.summary: ARTICLE XVI PHILIPPINE EAGLES CODE OF CONDUCT CHAPTER 1 MORAL CODE OF ETHICS
articles.content:
--- Page 176 ---
ARTICLE XVI
PHILIPPINE EAGLES CODE OF CONDUCT
CHAPTER 1
MORAL CODE OF ETHICS
SECTION 1. Every Eagle-member shall strictly adhere to the Philippine Eagles Ethical Code of Conduct, now popularly known as the Philippine Eagles Delicadeza and Moral Code of Ethics.
SECTION 2. As a declared policy, every Eagle-member shall uphold high standards of integrity and moral values, in dealing with both fellow Eagle and non-Eagles. No Eagle-member shall engage in immoral acts that could negatively impact, not only on the individual Eagle-member but more on the entire Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 3. Every Eagle-member shall treat fellow members as brothers, demonstrating utmost respect. He shall strive to support and uplift his fellow Eagle-members rather than bring them down.
In cases of misunderstanding, it shall be resolved in a gentleman manner, and their words are taken as Oath—solemn and binding.
SECTION 4. Every Eagle-member shall view others with compassion rather than eyes of condemnation. Every individual goes through different situations every day and only the person himself can know whether he is going through rough times or smooth days. An Eaglemember shall be sensitive to the feelings of others, whether a brother Eagle or a non-Eagle, as compassion fosters broader understanding and benevolence.
SECTION 5. No Eagle-member shall air his grievances on social media and other similar platforms. Eagle-member believes and has faith in the systems and processes of our Fraternity, as such, he shall course his complaints to the appropriate Grievance Tribunal Committee,

--- Page 177 ---
provided in this Philippine Eagles Constitution of 2024, allowing for due process and respecting the Committee’s decision.
SECTION 6. In line with Eagles Delicadeza, every Eagle-member shall take an Oath that he or she shall take no court action on any grievance against the Philippine Eagles, his Eagles Club, Region or his fellow Eagles without first exhausting administrative remedies. Based on each Eagle-member assessment of the situation or gravity of the matter, he shall be obliged to take a sporting gesture of delicadeza, to take a leave of absence from his region or club, or the Philippine Eagles, in case of irreconcilable conflict or difference with any of them. His leave of absence shall be construed as the ultimate redress of his or her grievance. After his leave of absence, he may return to the fold when the conflict has been resolved, after due notice to his region, club, or Philippine Eagles. This sporting gesture is without prejudice to the right of any Eagle-member to file appropriate criminal or civil action, when warranted.
CHAPTER 2
PHILIPPINE EAGLES DELICADEZA
SECTION 1. Philippine Eagles Delicadeza represents the moral high ground, maintaining high standards of respect, ethics, integrity, and decency in accordance with community norms and the ideals of Eagleism and the principles of the four pillars of Eagleism. Every Eagle-member’s actions should be guided by these principles, with the objective of offering prestige, respect and esteem to the Philippine Eagles.
SECTION 2. Eagles Delicadeza means acting properly in positions of authority, power, or trust. An Eagle-member shall not exploit their position to take advantage of fellow Eagle-members but should instead assist them embodying the concept of Alalayang Agila. Eaglemembers must maintain trust and confidence, using their position

--- Page 178 ---
to enhance their service to the Philippine Eagles, with all decisions and actions being decent and appropriate.
SECTION 3. Eagles Delicadeza also means adhering to generally accepted moral standards. As Eagle-members, individuals are expected to abide by the norms and morals upheld by the Philippine Eagles and the community.
SECTION 4. Eagles Delicadeza means doing the right thing, even when unobserved. Every Eagle-member is committed to practice proper decorum both publicly and privately, maintaining high moral principles and values that aim to bring honor to himself and to the Philippine Eagles.
CHAPTER 3
COMMON PROVISIONS
SECTION 1. The Philippine Eagles Code of Conduct is mandatory, ensuring the stability and unity of the Philippine Eagles. Since its establishment in 1979, the Philippine Eagles relies on the individual conscience of each and every Eagle-member for adherence.
SECTION 2. Each Eagles Club or Region may promulgate their own Moral Code of Conduct, but must be consistent with and subject to the provisions of this Article.
